CLOSED COUNCIL

In accordance with the Local Government Act 1993 and the Local Government (General) Regulation 2021, in the opinion of the General Manager, the following business is of a kind as referred to in Section 10A(2) of the Act, and should be dealt with in a part of the meeting closed to the media and public. 

 

17.1 Confidential Mayoral Minute - Appointment of General Manager

 

That Report, Confidential Mayoral Minute - General Manager Recruitment, be dealt with in Closed Council as it relates to Section 10A(2) of the Act being: 

 

  1. personnel matters concerning particular individuals (other than councillors)

 

23/05/06 RESOLVED (MOVED: Montgomery /SECONDED: COCHRANE)

 

  1. That Council resolve into closed council to consider business identified, tabled at the meeting.
  2. That pursuant under Section 10A(1)-(3) of the Local Government Act 1993, the media and public be excluded from the meeting on the basis that the business to be considered is classified confidential under the provisions of Section 10A(2) as outlined above.
  1. That the correspondence and reports relevant to the subject business be withheld from access to the media and public as required by Section 11(2) of the Local Government Act 1993.

 

The Council moved into closed Council at the time being 12.07pm.

  1. That Council appoint Kelvin Tytherleigh as General Manager of Moree Plains Shire Council on the following terms:
  • 5 year standard contract of employment as specified under the Local Government Act
  • A total remuneration package of $360,000 (cash and superannuation)
  • The provision of a private use motor vehicle including fuel
  • Provision of rental accommodation for a period of 6 months

  1. That the Mayor be provided delegated authority to negotiate the final terms of the contract using the Standard Contract of Employment for General Managers of Local Councils in NSW.

Should Council like to review, in detail, the confidential aspects of this report then this should be dealt with in ‘Closed Council’ as it relates to a section 10A(2) of the Local Government Act 1993 (NSW) (the Act).  Council will then need to resolve to move into ‘Closed Council’ with the explanation as follows:
 
That Attachment 1 of Report, Additional Advisory Committee Nominations - May 2023 (Confidential), be dealt with in Closed Council as it relates to Section 10A(2) of the Act being: 
 
(a) personnel matters concerning particular individuals (other than councillors) 

23/05/10 RESOLVED (MOVED: COCHRANE/SECONDED: SAUER) 

1.    That Council resolve into closed council to consider business identified, tabled at the meeting.

2.    That pursuant under Section 10A(1)-(3) of the Local Government Act 1993, the media and public be excluded from the meeting on the basis that the business to be considered is classified confidential under the provisions of Section 10A(2) as outlined above.

3.    That the correspondence and reports relevant to the subject business be withheld from access to the media and public as required by Section 11(2) of the Local Government Act 1993.
The Council moved into closed Council at the time being 2.43pm. The public and media left the Chamber.

1. That Council approve the Jacaranda Park Inclusive Playground Master Plan.
2. That Council endorse the submission of a variation request to NSW Department of Planning and Environment for the reallocation of Public Spaces Legacy Funding from Cooee Park to Jacaranda Park.
3. That additional funding be provided from the TED reserve totaling $327,831 to allow Stages 1 and 2 to be completed, with funding to be sought in the future for the construction of Stage 3.

1. That pursuant to Section 535 of the Local Government Act 1993 (the Act), Council hereby resolves to make the following rates and charges for the 2023/24 rating period:
 
a) Residential Rate 

Residential Ad Valorem rate (to apply to rateable land categorised as Residential within Moree Plains Shire in accordance with Section 516 of the Act) of 0.01150610 cents in the dollar and having a base rate of $500 per assessment (representing 17.48% of the total yield in accordance with Section 500 of the Act), yielding a total income of $4,532,321 in compliance with Council's allowable Notional Income.   
 
b) Residential Rural Rate 

Residential Rural Ad Valorem rate (to apply to all rateable land Sub-categorised Residential Rural within Moree Plains Shire in accordance with Section 529 (2)(b) of the Act) of 0.01150610 cents in the dollar and having a base rate of $500 per assessment (representing 2.46% of the total yield in accordance with Section 500 of the Act), yielding a total income of $639,020 in compliance with Council's allowable Notional Income.
 
c) Business Moree 

Business Moree Ad Valorem rate (to apply to all rateable land sub-categorised Business Moree within Moree Plains Shire in accordance with Section 529(2)(d) of the Act) of 0.03426829 cents in the dollar and having a base rate of $500 (representing 11.17% of the total yield in accordance with Section 500 of the Act), yielding a total income of $2,897,292 in compliance with Council’s allowable Notional Income.   

d) Business Rate

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"23/06/05 RESOLVED (MOVED: Mayor Johnson / SECONDED: Councillor Smith)
That: 

  1. Council writes to the Treasurer, the Minister for Emergency Services, the Minister for Local Government and local State Member(s):
      
    1. Expressing Council’s strong opposition to the NSW Government’s last minute decision to impose an enormous Emergency Services Levy (ESL) cost increase on councils for 2023/24 by scrapping the ESL subsidy for councils and at a time after Council has publicly advertised its Operational Plan and annual budget to the community;
       
    2. Noting that as a consequence of the unannounced 73% increase in the State Emergency Service budget and an 18% increase in the Fire and Rescue NSW budget, Council’s 3.7% rate increase to provide essential community services and infrastructure has been significantly eroded.
       
    3. Advising that the Government’s decision may/will lead to a reduction in important local services and/or the cancellation of necessary infrastructure projects;
       
    4. Calling on the NSW Government to take immediate action to:
  1. restore the ESL subsidy in 2023/24 
  2. urgently introduce legislation to decouple the ESL from the rate peg to enable councils to recover the full cost 
  3. develop a fairer, more transparent and financially sustainable method of funding critically important emergency services in consultation with local government.
 
2. Council writes to the Chair of the Independent Pricing and Regulatory Tribunal (IPART) advising that Council’s forced emergency services contribution is manifestly disproportionate to the 2023/24 rate cap, which has resulted in additional financial stress.
  
3. Council writes to the President of LGNSW seeking the Association’s ongoing advocacy to bring about a relief in the burden of Councils’ emergency services contribution.

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"That Council thank Tammy Elbourne for her 23 Years of Service to the Moree Community and wish Tammy all the best for her future endeavors. 

Born and bred in Moree, Tammy has always been passionate about our Shire.  Tammy and her team have been avid supporters and ambassadors of the Moree Plains Shire, and this has been reflected in the multiple awards won.
 
These include.
 
Regional Tourism Awards
 2010, 2012, 2013 – Inland Tourism Awards
 
 State Tourism Awards
 Recipients in 2013, 2014, 2015 
2015 – inducted into HALL OF FAME
 
 Australian Tourism Awards
 Finalist in 2013, 2014, 2015
 2013 - Australia Tourism Awards – Bronze Winner

 On behalf of our Community, I thank Tammy for her tireless efforts and the amazing passion and dedication to the Moree Plains.

That Council resolve:
1.    That an interim policy position be adopted for Section 64 water and sewer headworks developer contributions, including the following:
        i.    Section 64 charges to be applied as below:
              Water       $2,477.67 per Equivalent Tenement
              Sewer       $1,800.33 per Equivalent Tenement
These charges shall be capped until Council resolves an updated policy position.
      ii.    Subdivision development and residential accommodation on residential-zoned land is exempt from Section 64 developer contributions
      iii.    Section 64 developer contributions for infill development do not apply to development in the following circumstances: 
                 a. The site is within an urban land use zone in Moree Plains Shire; and
                 b. The site has existing direct access to Council water and sewer services; and
                 c. The site has previously been utilised for urban purposes, whether current or historic; and
                 d. The proposed development is for infill development or a change of land/building use; and
                 e. The site, if situated within the Moree Special Activation Precinct area, is a brownfield site only.
This position applies until such time as Council resolves an updated policy position having regard to the Council’s adopted Integrated Water Management Strategy. 

2.    If the site is not a brownfield site in the Moree Special Activation Precinct area and involves a high volume water user (>30 megalitres/annum) then a case by case assessment will be made to apply a charge. This position applies until such time as Council resolves an updated policy position having regard to the Council’s adopted Integrated Water Management Strategy.

3.    That a further report be brought to Council investigating the potential utilisation of water and sewer usage charges to assist in funding water and sewer infrastructure headworks

4.    That grant funding opportunities for water and sewer infrastructure headworks be explored.

5.    That usage-based Section 64 charges be made available for commercial or industrial development upon request, to provide an operational basis for determining contributions.

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"In accordance with the Local Government Act 1993 and the Local Government (General) Regulation 2021, in the opinion of the General Manager, the following business is of a kind as referred to in Section 10A(2) of the Act, and should be dealt with in a part of the meeting closed to the media and public. 

That Report, Confidential - Tender for the Construction of the Moree Artesian Aquatic Centre Redevelopment - Stage 1A, be dealt with in Closed Council as it relates to Section 10A(2) of the Act being:

(d)         commercial information of a confidential nature that would, if disclosed:
(i)          prejudice the commercial position of the person who supplied it, or
(ii)         confer a commercial advantage on a competitor of the council, or      
(iii)         reveal a trade secret 

23/10/02  RESOLVED (MOVED: Councillor Orchin / SECONDED: Councillor Montgomery)

1.    That Council resolve into closed council to consider business identified, tabled at the meeting.

2.    That pursuant under Section 10A(1)-(3) of the Local Government Act 1993, the media and public be excluded from the meeting on the basis that the business to be considered is classified confidential under the provisions of Section 10A(2) as outlined above.

3.    That the correspondence and reports relevant to the subject business be withheld from access to the media and public as required by Section 11(2) of the Local Government Act 1993.

The Council moved into closed Council at the time being 8.40am. The public and media left the Chamber. Cr Harting left the meeting 8.41am and did not return. Cr James closed the Teams link and entered the meeting in the chambers 8.51am. Cr Cochrane entered the meeting 9.04am and left 9.31am (via Teams). Nick Tobin left the meeting and did not return 9.15am.

23/10/04 RESOLVED (MOVED: Councillor Montgomery / SECONDED: Councillor Orchin)

That Council move into Open Council.
The Council moved into Open Council at the time being 9.49am.

The General Manager read out the following in open Council:

23/10/03 RESOLVED (MOVED: COUNCILLOR JAMES / SECONDED: DEPUTY MAYOR PEARSE)

  1. Council accepts the lump sum tender total of $9,917,626 Excl. GST submitted by Crystal Pools Pty Ltd ABN 81 002 172 063 based upon information provided to and considered by the Tender Panel for the construction of RFT22/544 Moree Artesian Aquatic Centre Redevelopment Stage 1A_Contract 1;
  2. Given the community interest in this Project, the Risk Managment Plan and Project Managment Plan associated with RFT22/544 Moree Artesian Aquatic Centre Redevelopment Stage 1A_Contract 1 between Moree Plains Shire Council and Crystal Pools Pty Ltd be executed under Council’s seal after all contract documents are subject to a Council Resolution. 
  3. That pursuant to section 377 of the Local Government Act 1993, the Council gives the General Manager subject to external legal advice delegated authority to execute the contract agreement between Moree Plains Shire Council and Crystal Pools Pty Ltd for RFT22/544 Moree Artesian Aquatic Centre Redevelopment Stage 1A_Contract 1.
  4. That details of the contract with Crystal Pools Pty Ltd be made public following exchange of letters between both parties accepting the terms agreed.
  5. That the proposed Risk and Project Management Plans be brought back to Council at a future Meeting of Council and be a part of the Public Meeting Documentation.
There being no further business, the meeting closed, the time being 09:52 AM

1. Note: Late Report 15.2 Accessible Parking near Moree Public School on Albert Street of the 21 September 2023 Ordinary Council Meeting was resolved on that day.

3. Note the concerns raised by Moree Public School Principal Mrs Sharyn  Cox.
 
4. Bring the Report Accessible Parking near Moree Public School on Albert Street back to Council at the 16 November 2023 Ordinary Council Meeting to allow for public consultation with all stakeholders.

6. Request Moree Public School consult internally and within its parent community as to the consensus and that data be provided to Council for inclusion in the 16 November 2023 Ordinary Council Meeting report.
 
7. Request Moree Public School include in their school newsletter parking expectations and requirements.

The General Manager read out the following in open Council:

23/11/21  RESOLVED (MOVED: COUNCILLOR MONTGOMERY / SECONDED: COUNCILLOR ORCHIN)

That Council: 
  1. Pursuant to section 55(3)(i) of the Local Government Act 1993, resolves not to invite tenders, as a satisfactory result would not be achieved due to extenuating circumstances, due to the facility remaining under redevelopment.
  2. That Moree Plains Shire Council extend the Moree Artesian Aquatic Centre (MAAC) management contract with Belgravia Health and Leisure Group from 1 July 2024 until 30 June 2027. 
  3. That Council approve the hosting of a Community Day Event, in conjunction with St Vincent de Paul Society and Belgravia, at the Moree Artesian Aquatics Centre (MAAC) on Sunday, 10 December 2023, commencing at 11am and concluding at 3pm, with the cost of holding the event being funded from the MAAC operational budget 2023/24.

23/11/22  RESOLVED (MOVED: COUNCILLOR ORCHIN / SECONDED: COUNCILLOR COCHRANE)

That Council:
 
  1. Sell Lot 2 DP 1263177, known as 114 Anne Street, Moree, to the Moree Sports Health Arts and education Academy Aboriginal Corporation (Indigenous Corporation Number: 8785), ABN: 39 580 339 005 and that all documents associated with the sale be executed under Council Seal.
 
  1. Formally provide notice to the Officer of Prime Minister and Cabinet that Council proposes to dispose of Lot 2 DP 1263177, known as 114 Anne Street, Moree to the Moree Sports Health Arts and education Academy Aboriginal Corporation (Indigenous Corporation Number: 8785), ABN: 39 580 339 005 and is providing them with 30 days notice of the same, in accordance with the Indigenous Grants – Tripartite Purposes Deed, dated 30 May 2018 and will therefore no longer be a party to this agreement.  

  1. Write-off the interest that has accrued on the lease payments for 114 Anne Street, Moree for the lease between Moree Plains Shire Council and the Moree Sports Health Arts and education Academy Aboriginal Corporation.
There being no further business, the meeting closed, the time being 04:55 PM

  1. That, Moree Plains Shire Council call on all members of the NSW Parliament to commit to bipartisan support to establish a Parliamentary Inquiry into and report on the rate of crime in all categories reported on by the Bureau of Crime Statistical and Research (BOCSAR) in Regional, Rural and Remote New South Wales, specifically focusing on the inequity between Metro and Regional Local Government areas. 
  2. That, Moree Plains Shire Council calls on all members of the NSW Parliament to commit to bipartisan support to increase spending on the NSW police force to increase front line policing numbers in Regional, Rural and Remote regions most at need.
  3. That, Moree Plains Shire Council call on the NSW Government to commit to the minimum staffing agreements (known in the NSW Police Force as First Response Agreements) for non-24 hour police stations, all of which are located in Regional, Rural and Remote Local Government areas.
  4. That, Moree Plains Shire Council calls on the NSW Government to review the current formula used to assess staffing levels including the universally agreed outdated current model for those Local Government areas that do have a First Response Agreement in place. 
Cr Cochrane requested her vote against the motion be recorded.

That Council:
  1. Endorse placing the draft Moree Plains Local Infrastructure Contributions Plan 2024 (draft Plan), incorporating provisions allowing Council to impose a levy on development within the Moree Special Activation Precinct (SAP) calculated at 3 per cent of the development cost over $200,000, on public exhibition for a minimum period of 42 days and invite public submissions during the exhibition period.
  2. Receive a further report following the exhibition and submission period addressing any submissions made in respect of the draft Plan. 
  3. Note that, subject to Council’s consideration of a report on the outcomes of the public exhibition, including any submission received, Council will need to make a request to the Minister for Planning and Public Space to approve the proposed levy above 1 per cent of the development cost within the Moree SAP.
  4. That Council engage directly with impacted businesses withing the SAP on the proposed contributions thresholds, noting the historical value of $200k.  
  5. Council provides delegated authority for the General Manager to negotiate and execute a 'Development Contributions Deed' between Moree Plains Shire Council and the NSW Regional Growth Development Corporation (RGDC) for the purposes of:
    1. Establishing a framework for determining how required Contributions (as per the aforementioned Local Infrastructure Contributions Plan 2024) will be collected and remitted to RGDC in respect of the Moree SAP
    2. Facilitating the delivery of the Infrastructure Works by RGDC within the Moree SAP.

 That:
  1. Council reasserts that the Moree Intermodal Overpass (MIO/"The Overpass") is a critical component of the approved Inland Rail project and is of the highest strategic importance to the Moree Special Activation Precinct, the Moree Plains economy, and the safety and amenity of the Moree township. 
  2. Council progresses representations and meetings with The Hon. Anthony Albanese MP, Prime Minister, The Hon. Chris Minns MP, NSW Premier, relevant Federal and State ministers and departments to stress the criticality of the project and progress solutions for its delivery.  
  3.  Council seeks written assurance from ARTC Inland Rail that an overpass remains a condition of approval for the Narrabri to Northstar SP1 project noting Council has not given any form of consent to remove this condition of approval.
  4. Council expresses its strong opposition to the Australian Government’s decision to cut significant infrastructure funding from important projects across NSW including the Moree Intermodal Overpass,
  5. Noting that the infrastructure funding cuts will hamper the ability of communities to accommodate growth and increased housing supply, and harm productivity improvements required for the growing freight task
  6. Calling for the Australian Government to reinstate funding for these critical infrastructure projects.5.  Council writes to the Hon Chris Minns MP, NSW Premier, seeking the NSW Government’s support for joint advocacy on this matter to the Australian Government.

In accordance with the Local Government Act 1993 and the Local Government (General) Regulation 2021, in the opinion of the General Manager, the following business is of a kind as referred to in Section 10A(2) of the Act, and should be dealt with in a part of the meeting closed to the media and public. 

18.1. NOTICE OF MOTION TO RESCIND A COUNCIL RESOLUTION

(a)      personnel matters concerning particular individuals (other than councillors),
(b)      the personal hardship of any resident or ratepayer,
(c)      information that would, if disclosed, confer a commercial advantage on a person with whom the council is conducting (or proposes to conduct) business,
(d)      commercial information of a confidential nature that would, if disclosed:
(i)       prejudice the commercial position of the person who supplied it, or
(ii)      confer a commercial advantage on a competitor of the council, or    
(iii)     reveal a trade secret,
(e)      information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law,
(f)       matters affecting the security of the council, councillors, council staff or council property,
(g)      advice concerning litigation, or advice that would otherwise be privileged from production in legal proceedings on the ground of legal professional privilege,
(h)      information concerning the nature and location of a place or an item of Aboriginal significance on community land,
(i)      alleged contraventions of any code of conduct requirements applicable under section 440.


24/01/04   RESOLVED (MOVED:  Councillor Montgomery /SECONDED: Councillor Orchin) 

1.    That Council move into closed council to consider business identified, tabled at the meeting.
2.    That pursuant under Section 10A(1)-(3) of the Local Government Act 1993, the media and public be excluded from the meeting on the basis that the business to be considered is classified confidential under the provisions of Section 10A(2) as outlined above.
3.    That the correspondence and reports relevant to the subject business be withheld from access to the media and public as required by Section 11(2) of the Local Government Act 1993.

The Council moved into closed Council at the time being 11:00 AM. The public and media left the Chamber.

RECOMMENDATION

That Council:
  1. Endorses Council being the provider for the Mungindi Community Daycare and Mobile Daycare.
  2. Accepts the Community Childcare Fund Grant to build and commence operations at a new daycare facility upon the condition that Council contribute not more than the $50,000.00 already committed to the required $300,000.00 co-contribution.
  3. Agrees to build and operate a new daycare facility on the corner of Bucknell & Wall Street, Mungindi.

24/01/02  RESOLVED (MOVED: Councillor Sauer / SECONDED: Councillor Montgomery)

That Council: 
  1. Recognises the critical importance of a permanent early years childcare service to the livability, economy and sustainability of the Mungindi community,
  2. Investigates options for a permanent childcare solution in Mungindi in partnership with Balonne Shire Council, Mungindi Progress Association and other relevant organisations and businesses,
  3. Develops a project plan, budget and long term cost benefit analysis, in conjunction with project partners, to be considered at a future Committe Meeting at the earliest convenience.
  4. Continue efforts to obtain registration and certification for the mobile daycare. 

Cr James left the meeting the time being 9:45 AM and did not return.
Cr Cochrane left the meeting the time being 10:00 AM and did not return.

That there be a short break in the meeting.
The break in the meeting began at the time being 10.22 AM and resumed the time being 10:29 AM.

24/01/05  RESOLVED (MOVED: COUNCILLOR SAUER / SECONDED: DEPUTY MAYOR PEARSE)

 MOTION:
  1. That pursuant to section 178(1)(b) of the Local Government (General) Regulation 2021 (NSW) Council declines to accept any of the submissions received for the construction of RFT22/544 Moree Artesian Aquatic Centre Redevelopment Stage 1A Contract 2. 
  2. That pursuant to section 178(3)(e) of the Local Government (General) Regulation 2021 (NSW) Council resolves to negotiate with suitably qualified firms to procure the completion of the construction works contemplated by RFT22/544 Moree Artesian Aquatic Centre Redevelopment Stage 1A Contract 2.
  3. That Council’s reasons for declining to invite fresh tender submissions or applications in respect of RFT22/544 Moree Artesian Aquatic Centre Redevelopment Stage 1A Contract 2 are that proceeding otherwise is:
    1. likely to unduly delay commencement of the required works;
    2. is unlikely to produce submissions or applications additional to, or more advantageous to Council than, those received in response to RFT22/544; and
    3. is not in the best interests of the community.
  4. That Council’s reasons for determining to enter into negotiations with suitably qualified firms to procure the completion of the construction works contemplated by RFT22/544 Moree Artesian Aquatic Centre Redevelopment Stage 1A Contract 2 is that this is considered the most advantageous means of securing suitably qualified firms to undertake the required works to the standard and timeline required by Council. 
  5. That pursuant to section 377 of the Local Government Act 1993 (NSW), Council gives the General Manager delegated authority to negotiate and execute any contract agreements for the Moree Artesian Aquatic Centre Redevelopment including earthworks, piling, clubhouse, covered seating and grandstand.

That;

That the General Manager prepares the draft 2024-2025 budget in accordance with the following principles:
  1. A focus on getting back to basics, prioritising core statutory service delivery and completion of grant-funded projects.
  2. That in order to address long term underfunding and poor condition of Council’s rural road network, annual expenditure on rural roads is increased to 68% of Council’s annual rate revenue, excluding grant funding.
  3. All fees and charges increase in line with the Consumer Price Index, except in circumstances where Council’s fees and charges are not in line with comparable large rural Councils or are not providing a break even return. In these instances, the General Manager should provide specific recommendations back to the Council.
  4. That provision is made for adequate, qualified project management resources to complete all proposed projects that are required to be completed in FY2024-2025 as per grant funding deeds or variations approved by the funding body.
  5. That in accordance with s332 of the Local Government Act 1993, the organisation structure is reviewed by the General Manager in consultation with the Council, and recommendations made to the Council in order to ensure the workforce is resourced to meet these priorities.
  6. That the General Manager considers all recommendations of the Council-commissioned July 2022 AEC Service Level Review and NSW Group 11 Councils Service Benchmarking Report in reviewing the organisation structure and staffing levels

That: 
  1. In accordance with section 38D of the Roads Act 1993 (NSW), Council approve closing of the public road laneway within section 1, village of Gurley, shown as Lots 1 and 2 on Diagram “X” attached. 
  2. Upon closure the subject road will vest in Council as Operational land pursuant to Section 43(2) of the Roads Act 1993 (NSW).
  3. Land in the closed road is to be defined in plans of survey and be disposed of to the adjoining owners in accordance with Council’s Land Acquisition and Disposal Policy.
  4. That easements for water supply and sewerage services be created to support existing services affecting Lot 2 in the plan of definition for road closing purposes.
  5. A plan be prepared for the purpose of consolidation of the closed road in Lot 1 with the surrounding Lot 20, DP 1225687
  6. An Easement for Water Supply be created in the plan of consolidation of land of closed road (Lot 1) and Lot 20, DP 1225687 to support the relocation of the existing water supply pipeline within the development site.
  7. The purchase prices listed in the confidential section of this report be approved for Lot 1 and Lot 2.
  8. All documents associated with the closing, easement creation and sale be settled by the General Manager and executed under Council seal.

(b)        the personal hardship of any resident or ratepayer

The Council moved into closed Council. The public and media left the Chamber.

2024/5/21  RESOLVED (MOVED: Deputy Mayor Pearse / SECONDED: Councillor Cochrane)

In accordance with the Local Government Act 1993 and the Local Government (General) Regulation 2021, in the opinion of the General Manager, the following business is of a kind as referred to in Section 10A(2) of the Act, and should be dealt with in a part of the meeting closed to the media and public. 

Should the Council wish to further consider the Sale of Land for Unpaid Rates 2023 they will need to resolve with the explanation as follows:
 
That Report – Confidential – Sale of Land for Unpaid Rates, be dealt with in Closed Council as it relates to Section 10A (2)(b) of the Local Government Act 1993 being:
 
            (d)        The personal hardship of any resident or ratepayer
 
The current negotiations for the sale of land for unpaid rates are confidential in nature and it is not in the public interest to reveal this information as it may prejudice the Council.

1.    That Council move into closed council to consider business identified, tabled at the meeting.

2.    That pursuant under Section 10A(1)-(3) of the Local Government Act 1993, the media and public be excluded from the meeting on the basis that the business to be considered is classified confidential under the provisions of Section 10A(2) as outlined above.

3.    That the correspondence and reports relevant to the subject business be withheld from access to the media and public as required by Section 11(2) of the Local Government Act 1993.
The Council moved into closed Council at the time being 3.55pm. The public and media left the Chamber.

The General Manager read out the following in open Council:

2024/5/22  RESOLVED (MOVED: COUNCILLOR MONTGOMERY / SECONDED: DEPUTY MAYOR PEARSE)

  1. That Council implements proceedings to sell the properties listed in this report at a public auction at a time and place to be determined, pursuant to Section 713 and other relevant sections of the Local Government Act 1993 and regulations.
  2. That The Centre for Sustainable Debt Recovery Pty Ltd (Recoupa) be appointed to administer the sale on Council’s behalf.
  3. That Council authorises the General Manager to proceed with the necessary arrangements pertaining to the sale of the properties listed in this report, as set out in the Local Government Act 1993 and Local Government (General) Regulation 2021.
  4. Advertisements for the auction be placed in the 'NSW Government Gazette', 'The Moree Champion', Council's website and Council's Facebook page. The advertisement must conform to the provisions of Section (715)1 of the Local Government Act.

  6. That Council authorises the General Manager  to execute contracts and transfer documents pertaining to the properties specified in the body of the report.
  7. That Council reserves the right to withdraw the property from sale for technical or legal reasons.

There being no further business, the meeting closed, the time being 04:03 PM

OPEN COUNCIL

That Council moves into Open Council.
The General Manager read out the following in open Council:


REPORT 18.1 - Confidential - Annual Debt Write off 2023/2024

     2024/6/11 RESOLVED (MOVED: Councillor Smith / SECONDED: Councillor Sauer)

1. That Council writes off the Bad Debt Writes, as detailed in Tables A, totaling $39,112.24 accordance with Council’s Debt Write Policy and the Local Government (General) Regulation 2021 (NSW) Clause 213. 
2. That Table B be received for information as the debts totaling $11,059.44 has been written off under delegation. 
3. That a budget variation of $25,171.68 is requested to account for unforeseen non-recoverable debts. 

REPORT 18.2 - Confidential - Moree Artesian Aquatic Centre Redevelopment - Growing Regions Grand and pool fencing.

     RESOLVED  2024/6/12 (MOVED: Councillor Sauer / SECONDED: Councillor Montgomery)

That Council:
  1. Approve one of the following scope of works and related costs for the Moree Artesian Aquatic Centre redevelopment:
    1. An amended scope that removes the ‘Learn to Swim Pool’ from the Moree Artesian Aquatic Centre redevelopment, with the exception of structural pilings and/or footings for the ‘Learn to Swim Pool’ to allow for potential future completion of this asset, with a reduction in the currently proposed borrowings from $7M to $3M.
  2. Approve delegated authority for the General Manager to execute the Growing Regions Program grant deed.
 
REPORT 18.3 - Confidential Tender RFT24/03 Design and Construction Ashley Water Supply.

     2024/6/13 RESOLVED (MOVED: Councillor Montgomery / SECONDED: Councillor Sauer)

  1. That the General Manager notifies Restart NSW that Moree Plains Shire Council is declining Deed offer RNSW830.
  2. That the Community are informed of this decision with a formal letter to all landowners in the Village of Ashley.   
 
REPORT 18.4 - Confidential RFT21/03 Casual Plant, Watercarts and Tipping Trucks Hire & RFT21/13 Supply of Plant and Labour for Flood Recovery Work for MPSC.

     2024/6/15 RESOLVED (MOVED: Councillor Montgomery / SECONDED: Councillor SMITH)

  1. That Council, after considering the responses received to RFT21/13, decline all tenders under section 178(1)(b) of the Local Government (General) Regulation 2021 (NSW) and cancel the proposal for the contract.
  2. That Council approve the addition of contractors to the Casual Plant, Watercart and Tipping Truck Hire pre-qualified panel as detailed in Attachment one.

REPORT 18.5 Confidential - Code of Conduct Breach - Consideration of Final Investigation Report

     2024/6/37 RESOLVED (MOVED: COUNCILLOR MONTGOMERY / SECONDED: DEPUTY MAYOR PEARSE)

That the Report be deferred to a future Ordinary Council Meeting.

d) Business Rate

e) Farmland Rate

f) Mining

2024/6/34 RESOLVED (MOVED: Councillor Cochrane / SECONDED: Councillor Montgomery)


That Council approve Development Application 2023/80 for a 34-lot residential subdivision at 281 Edward Street Moree, subject to the conditions of development consent in Attachment 1 to this report and the following additional and/or amended conditions:
 
RESTRICTIONS 
Identified in Part 1 of the 88B Instrument as: “Restriction on the use of land” 
All relevant Section 88B restrictions and covenants created, as part of this consent shall contain a provision that they cannot be extinguished or altered except with the consent of Moree Plains Shire Council.
 
Onsite Stormwater Detention Systems
An appropriate restriction on the use of the land/covenant shall be created under Section 88B of the Conveyancing Act 1919 as follows:
1.  No dwelling or other structure shall be erected or constructed unless the registered proprietor(s) have constructed or make provision for the construction of an On-site Detention system on the said lot(s) that controls the surface runoff from the lot, including all pervious and impervious surfaces and limits the stormwater discharge to the inter allotment drainage system, public road drainage system or natural drainage system to match the pre development site discharge condition for all critical storm events up to and including the 100 year ARI event
2.  Roofs and gutters are designed to maximise the capture of rainwater, up to the 100 year ARI storm event, to the On-Site detention system.
3.  On-Site detention system shall be connected to a piped drainage system or public road drainage system.
 
RAINWATER TANKS 
An appropriate restriction on the use of the land/covenant shall be created under Section 88B of the Conveyancing Act 1919 as follows:
  1. No dwelling shall be constructed on the lot(s) hereby burdened unless the registered proprietor has first constructed or has made provision for the construction of a rainwater tank with a minimum capacity of 5,000 litres in accordance with the requirements of Moree Plains Shire Council.
FENCING 
An appropriate restriction on the use of the land/covenant shall be created under Section 88B of the Conveyancing Act 1919 as follows:
  1. All fencing erected on side and rear property boundaries behind the building alignment, shall be a ‘Colorbond’ style metal fence, be Colorbond ‘Evening Haze’ colour and be 1.8 metre high.
  2. Any boundary retaining walls (including current and proposed boundaries) are to be of masonry construction. Retaining walls are to have a maximum single height of 1.2 m. Any retaining walls over 1.2 m are to be stepped with minimum 900 mm distance between steps and sufficient landscaping within the 900 mm gap.
  3. All fencing is to be erected on top of any retaining walls at full cost to the developer. 
 STREET TREE PLANTING
The applicant must submit a Landscape Plan detailing the proposed street tree planting and landscaping for the approved subdivision. The Street Tree Plan is to reflect the species palette in our Street Tree Guidelines and must include:
  • Species
  • details of root protection barriers
  • soil specifications
  • location of tree pits in relation to services, intersections and future driveways,
  • light poles, stormwater pits sewerage infrastructure and utilities
Street tree planting must not interfere with the street light spill. The applicant is to provide documentation to confirm there is no conflict between proposed vegetation at maturity and street lighting.

The Landscape Plan must include measures, such as landscaping and physical barriers, to prevent access by vehicles/motorbikes between the proposed subdivision roads and Edward Street.
For: Mayor Cr Johnson, Deputy Mayor Cr Pearse, Cr Sauer, Cr Hartin, Cr Orchin, Cr Smith, Cr Cochrane, Cr Montgomery    Against: Cr James.

2024/6/40 RESOLVED (MOVED: Deputy Mayor Pearse / SECONDED: Councillor Sauer)

  1. That Council has considered all tabled public submissions and community consultation made in relation to the Draft Operational Plan and Budget 2024-25 and Delivery Program 2024-26 Update, and Draft Long-Term Financial Plan 2024-34 and that the following changes be made:
a)  That Council continue to work towards the memorial for the Waterloo Creek Massacre.
b)  That Council add the CBD Masterplan
c)  That Council note the customer service response for the surrounding villages
d)  That add promoting Alcohol-free Events be included
e)  That Council add Community Safety Strategy and the Youth Strategy.

  1. That Council adopt the Operational Plan and Budget 2024-25 and Delivery Program 2024-26 Update, and the Long-Term Financial Plan 2024-34 with the following amendments:
a) Roads To Recovery
  1. Increase the budgeted capital revenue from $1,800,000.00 to $3,194,213.00
  2. Increase the budgeted capital expenditure from $1,800,000.00 to $3,194,213.00 (an increase of $1,394,213.00)
  3. That the allocation of this increase to budgeted capital expenditure of $1,394,213.00 be subject to a further report to Council
b)  Ashley Water Project - Remove the total project
  1. Remove the budgeted Capital Revenue of $3,962,993.00
  2. Remove the budgeted Capital Expenditure $6,972,412.00
  3. Remove the proposed borrowings of $2,900,000.00
  4. Remove the budgeted principal and interest loan repayments
     
  1. Moree Artesian Aquatic Centre – MAAC Project
a) Increase the budgeted capital revenue to include Growing Regional Program Grant $9,641,761.00                                                                                                                  
b) Remove the Learn to Swim Pool
  1. Amend the budgeted capital expenditure to a total of $25,676,610.72 ($23,666,610.72 in 2024-2025 and $2,010,000 in 2025/2026)
  2. Reduce the proposed borrowings from $7.0m to $3.0m
  3. Reduce budgeted principal and interest loan repayments to reflect the decrease in borrowings
c) Gwydir Daycare
  1. The budget be updated to reflect any changes to GDC fees and charges in point 4

  1. That Council resolves the following costs, included in the Operational Plan and Budget, be funded from the listed internal or external reserves:                                    
a. That the following costs be funded from the Tourism and Economic Development Fund Internal Reserve:
  1. Moree Artesian Aquatic Centre - $250,000.00
  2. Tourism Funding - $50,000.00
  3. Tourism Projects - $40,000.00
  4. RAU Projects - $140,000.00 (My Moree $25,000, Events Partnership Fund $20,000, Annual Business Micro Funding $20,000, Moree Plains Employee/Workforce Attraction Plan $75,000)

Include the breakdown by project
  1. Moree Hall Signature Event - $50,000.00
  2. Industrial Drive Loan Repayment - $117,130.00
  3. That the following costs be funded from the Road Reserve:
  4. Flood Recovery Betterment - $2,300.000.00
  5. North south Link - $1,278,634.00
  6. That the following costs be funded from the MAAC Reserve:
  7. Moree Artesian Aquatic Centre - balance of the reserve as at 01 July 2024    
  8. That the following costs be funded from the Aerodrome Reserve:
  9. Moree Airport reseal runway - $300,000.00
  10. That the following costs be funded from the Ron Harborne Reserve:  
  11. Ron Harborne Oval Redevelopment- $175,000.00                                      
  12. That the following costs be funded from the Environmental Protection Reserve:
  13. Dilapidated Properties Clean-up and Enforcement ($10k waste fee subsidy x 12 estimated properties) - $120,000.00
                 
  1. That Council adopt all tabled changes to the Fees and Charges Change Listing.
  1. That Council note the OP Plan include an increase of 17 FTE to Councils Human Resources and as per discussion with the General Manager this is expected to increase Councils level of Service to the Community and Delivery of Projects with an expectation of meeting 90% of all actions at year end.

 
2024/6/47 RESOLVED (MOVED: Deputy Mayor Pearse / SECONDED: Councillor Sauer)

2024/6/45 RESOLVED (MOVED: Councillor Smith / SECONDED: Councillor Montgomery)

That Council:
  1. Endorse the establishment of a permanent Community Childcare facility at Mungindi.
  2. Delegates authority to the General Manager to:
    1. confirm that MCEA are prepared to take over the operation of the childcare facility by the end of December 2026, at the latest, and to administer this transfer of provider from Council to MCEA. Conditional upon MCEA entering into a binding agreement with Moree Plains Shire Council. 
    2. verify that MCEA is financially able to provide the funding of $300,000.00 to meet the co-contribution requirement of the CCCF grant. 
    3. determine whether a consortium arrangement with MCEA constitutes a Public Private Partnership. (PPP)
      1. determine that the CCCF capital grant funding can be modified to include MCEA in a consortium arrangement as the owner of the childcare building.
      2. confirm that MCEA are prepared to accept the responsibility of ownership, construction/renovation of a building in a consortium arrangement with Council.            
  3. Agree to operate Mungindi Community Childcare as the approved provider for a maximum of 2 years whilst MCEA obtains approval to be a registered childcare provider. The operation of this facility will be supported by the $600,000.00 operational component of the CCCF grant which will assist this facility to run at no cost to Council.

2024/7/6 RESOLVED (MOVED: Councillor Cochrane / SECONDED: Deputy Mayor Pearse)

That Council,

1. Acknowledge the creation, enforcement and impact of the 1955 by-laws reinforcing racial segregation.
2. Holds an event at the Moree Artesian Aquatic Centre commemorating the 60th anniversary of the Freedom Rides in 20 February 2025; 
3. Provide free entry to the Moree Artesian Aquatic Centre on the day of the event Thursday 20 February 2025 with consideration of reduced rate from Friday 21 February to Sunday 23 February 2025. (That a future Report to Council be tabled at a future Ordinary Council Meeting to finalise details and funding allocation)
4. Annually commemorate the Freedom Rides on 20 February.
5. Invites representatives from the Moree Aboriginal community to form a working group for the event;

In accordance with the Local Government Act 1993 and the Local Government (General) Regulation 2021, in the opinion of the General Manager, the following business is of a kind as referred to in Section 10A(2) of the Act, and should be dealt with in a part of the meeting closed to the media and public. 

(a)      personnel matters concerning particular individuals (other than councillors),
(b)      the personal hardship of any resident or ratepayer,
(c)      information that would, if disclosed, confer a commercial advantage on a person with whom the council is conducting (or proposes to conduct) business,
(d)      commercial information of a confidential nature that would, if disclosed:
(i)       prejudice the commercial position of the person who supplied it, or
(ii)      confer a commercial advantage on a competitor of the council, or    
(iii)     reveal a trade secret,
(e)      information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law,
(f)       matters affecting the security of the council, councillors, council staff or council property,
(g)      advice concerning litigation, or advice that would otherwise be privileged from production in legal proceedings on the ground of legal professional privilege,
(h)      information concerning the nature and location of a place or an item of Aboriginal significance on community land,
(i)      alleged contraventions of any code of conduct requirements applicable under section 440.

1.    That Council move into closed council to consider business identified, tabled at the meeting.

2.    That pursuant under Section 10A(1)-(3) of the Local Government Act 1993, the media and public be excluded from the meeting on the basis that the business to be considered is classified confidential under the provisions of Section 10A(2) as outlined above.

3.    That the correspondence and reports relevant to the subject business be withheld from access to the media and public as required by Section 11(2) of the Local Government Act 1993.

1. That the General Manager, Mayor, Deputy Mayor and Councillor attends the Local Government NSW (LG NSW) Annual Conference to be held at Tamworth Regional Entertainment and Conference Centre from 17 November 2024 to 19 November 2024.
2. Endorse the Deputy Mayor as the second voting delegate along with the Mayor at the 2024 LGNSW Conference.  

3. That Council endorse the below motion to put forward to the LG NSW Annual Conference, motion due to the LGNSW Friday, 16 August 2024.

Motion subjectInland Rail 
MotionCall for the completion of the Inland Rail Narrabri to North Star 22km “missing link” of rail track that will support connection of the Moree Special Activation Precinct and agribusiness to ports across south eastern Australia. 
 
 Call for completion of the Inland Rail program from Brisbane to Melbourne in its entirety, to support growth and development across regional Australia.
National ObjectiveThis year the recommended motion aims to highlight the continuation and completion of Inland Rail construction within the Moree Plains and from Melbourne to Brisbane more broadly to support positive economic outcomes for the nation.
Summary of Key ArgumentsThe ‘missing link’ 22km rail link is still to be completed for the Narrabri to North Star (N2NS) section of track within the Moree Plains Shire, which is of critical importance to local agricultural businesses, the Moree Special Activation Precinct (SAP), and the national economy. 
 
 The N2NS project has been partially completed, falling short of Moree from Tapscott Road to Camurra, classified as Section 2C and N2NS Phase 2 projects. With the rail line incomplete, existing road-based supply chains will remain, which is more expensive, less efficient, and less safe.

That Council:
1. hold an election for the office of Mayor;
2. the vote is to be by ordinary ballot. 
3. declare the term of the Mayor be two years from the date of election as Mayor, per section 230(1) of the Local Government Act 1993 (NSW); and 
4. direct the General Manager to destroy all ballot papers following the declaration of the office of Mayor.

2024/10/5  RESOLVED (MOVED: Councillor Sauer / SECONDED: Councillor Pearse)

That there be a short break in the meeting.
The break in the meeting began at the time being 10.21am and resumed the time being  10.25am. 
The General Manager called for nominations. The General Manager received Nominations for Cr Pearse, James and Cassells. 

All candidates were given the opportunity to address the Council. Cr Cassells and Cr Pearse reserved the right to speak 

VOTE: 1
The General Manager drew lots to determine the order the Mayoral Candidates appeared on the ballet, listed below in this.  
Vote for Councillor James: 3
Vote for Councillor Pearse: 4
Vote for Councillor Cassells: 2
VOTE: 2
The General Manager drew lots to determine the order the Mayoral Candidates appeared on the ballet, listed below in this.  
Vote for Councillor James: 3
Vote for Councillor Pearse: 6
Note: The General Manager announced that the Mayor of Moree Plains Shire Council is Councillor Pearse for 2024/2026.
Mayor Pearse commenced the role as chair. Mayor Pearse addressed the Council and thanked the Council for their support.

2024/10/14 RESOLVED (MOVED: Councillor Cassells / SECONDED: Councillor Tighe)

That Council:
  1. notes section 291A(1)(b) of the Local Government Act 1993 (the Act) concerning the filling of certain casual vacancies occurring in the office of a Councillor by way of a countback of votes cast at the 2024 Local Government Election; 
  2. resolves that casual vacancies occurring in the office of a Councillor within 18 months after the last ordinary election of Councillors for the Council on 14 September 2024 are to be filled by a by-election for the office in accordance with section 291 of the Act; 
  3. directs the General Manager to notify the election manager of the Council’s decision within seven (7) days of the decision;
  4. provides feedback the NSW Electoral Commission on the conduct of the 2024 Local Government NSW Election in the Moree Plains; and 
  5. notes the cost of a by-election is to be met by budget savings and hence no additional cost to the community.

  • Cr Hodgkinson declared a non-significant non-pecuniary interest report 16.13 as her private business Property Excellence is a financial member of the Chamber of Commerce.

That Report, 'Confidential - Transfer of building 19 Airport Drive, Moree', be dealt with in Closed Council as it relates to Section 10A(2) of the Act being: 
 
(d)commercial information of a confidential nature that would, if disclosed: 

(i)      prejudice the commercial position of the person who supplied it, or

1.    That Council move into closed council to consider business identified, tabled at the meeting.

2.    That pursuant under Section 10A(1)-(3) of the Local Government Act 1993, the media and public be excluded from the meeting on the basis that the business to be considered is classified confidential under the provisions of Section 10A(2) as outlined above.

3.    That the correspondence and reports relevant to the subject business be withheld from access to the media and public as required by Section 11(2) of the Local Government Act 1993.

The Council moved into closed Council at the time being 01.40pm. The public and media left the Chamber.

In accordance with the Local Government Act 1993 and the Local Government (General) Regulation 2021, in the opinion of the General Manager, the following business is of a kind as referred to in Section 10A(2) of the Act, and should be dealt with in a part of the meeting closed to the media and public.

1.    That Council move into closed council to consider business identified, tabled at the meeting.

3.    That the correspondence and reports relevant to the subject business be withheld from access to the media and public as required by Section 11(2) of the Local Government Act 1993.

The Council moved into Closed Council the time being 4.19pm. The public and the media left the Chamber.

In accordance with the Local Government Act 1993 and the Local Government (General) Regulation 2021, in the opinion of the General Manager, the following business is of a kind as referred to in Section 10A(2) of the Act, and should be dealt with in a part of the meeting closed to the media and public. 

(a)      personnel matters concerning particular individuals (other than councillors),
(b)      the personal hardship of any resident or ratepayer,
(c)      information that would, if disclosed, confer a commercial advantage on a person with whom the council is conducting (or proposes to conduct) business,
(d)      commercial information of a confidential nature that would, if disclosed:
(i)       prejudice the commercial position of the person who supplied it, or
(ii)      confer a commercial advantage on a competitor of the council, or    
(iii)     reveal a trade secret,
(e)      information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law,
(f)       matters affecting the security of the council, councillors, council staff or council property,
(g)      advice concerning litigation, or advice that would otherwise be privileged from production in legal proceedings on the ground of legal professional privilege,
(h)      information concerning the nature and location of a place or an item of Aboriginal significance on community land,
(i)      alleged contraventions of any code of conduct requirements applicable under section 440.

1.    That Council move into closed council to consider business identified, tabled at the meeting.

2.    That pursuant under Section 10A(1)-(3) of the Local Government Act 1993, the media and public be excluded from the meeting on the basis that the business to be considered is classified confidential under the provisions of Section 10A(2) as outlined above.

3.    That the correspondence and reports relevant to the subject business be withheld from access to the media and public as required by Section 11(2) of the Local Government Act 1993.

The Council moved into closed Council at the time being 01:27pm. The public and media left the Chamber.

That the: 
1. Quarter 1 report on progress in implementing Moree Plains Shire Council's Operational Plan 2024-25 and Delivery Program 2024-26 be adopted and placed on Council's website.
2. That Council resolve to make the following changes in the Operational Plan 2024-25 and Delivery Program 2024-26:

Add Actions:
  • As per variations detailed in Attachment 1 of the QBRS report.
  • 2.2.3.34 "Seal the remaining 6.3km of Caloona Rd", with Performance Target: "Obtain grant funding and seal road", with End Date, "30 June 2026."
    Change Actions:
  • 4.1.3.11 "Enforce Local laws", with Performance Target "Compliance operations undertaken across the Shire consistently with Council Compliance and Enforcement Policy" to "Implement a Local Approvals Policy to streamline the approvals process for activities prescribed under the Local Government Act", with Performance Target "Compliance with the criteria set out in the Local Approvals Policy". (Council currently has no Local Laws specific to the Moree Plains Shire to enforce.)
  • 3.1.1.6 "Monitoring and controlling of weed threats to the Gwydir Wetland Ramsar sites under Local Land Services funding" to "Monitoring and controlling of weed threats to the Gwydir Wetland Ramsar sites under Funding" (Funding changed).
  • 4.2.1.1 "Produce and distribute information about Council decisions and activities to a range of audiences through a variety of channels", with Performance Target " Monthly Clipboards in Moree Champion and paid advertising triskins as required. 10 x 15 media releases issued per quarter, 90 x social media posts per quarter" to "Will advertise monthly with Moree Online News. Advertising with Moree Champion online as required. 10 x 15 media releases issued per quarter, 90 x social media posts per quarter" (Moree Champion no longer distributes printed copy).
Discontinue Actions:
  • 1.1.1.8 Procure a Mobile Stage Trailer for community events across the Shire. Recommend this project be discontinued, there was originally $60,000 in an early budget process. Council will continue to look for grant opportunities.
  • 1.1.3.5 Work with industry and Tourism Moree to initiate a feasibility study and plan for the commercial development of high-end artesian water products and tourist attractions. Staff recommend that Council consider discontinuing this project for the current FY and recommence efforts from FY25/26 to align with redevelopment of the Moree Artesian Aquatic Centre.
  • 2.2.2.12 Replace the non-directional beacon at Moree Airport FY23/24 Rollover. It is recommended this project be discontinued as this project is not Council's responsibility.
  • 2.3.1.2 Support and work with UNE to deliver the UNE Moree Plan. UNE have requested time to review the UNE Moree Plan in light of new leadership, as their new Vice Chancellor started last year. Council staff are recommending that Council consider postponing this action for this financial year and will look to recommence formal discussions with UNE in FY25/26.
  • 2.3.2.1 Finalise and implement Moree Plains Workforce Attraction and Retention Strategy in partnership with NSW Government. Staff recommend that Council consider postponing this action as current staffing efforts are focused on delivering the Welcome Experience Program for Moree Plains for FY 24/25 (Action 2.3.2.2). Welcome and settlement activities are a key pillar of the Moree Plains Workforce Attraction and Retention Strategy.
  • 3.1.6.22 Hydraulic analysis and design for stormwater management to support future development for the local housing strategy and Special Activation Precinct (SAP) (Carry over project FY23/24). Recommend this be discontinued to future financial years until finalisation of the SAP and urban release areas.

2024/12/42 RESOLVED (MOVED: Councillor Tighe / SECONDED: Councillor Sauer)

That Council:
  1. notes Report 19.2 “Confidential - Moree Artesian Aquatic Centre Redevelopment _ Contract 3” presented at the Ordinary Council Meeting of 12 December 2024 (Confidential Report);
  2. resolves that because of extenuating circumstances and the unavailability of competitive or reliable tenderers, a satisfactory result would not be achieved by inviting tenders for the engagement of a head contractor for the Moree Artesian Aquatic Centre Redevelopment (Proposed Contract);
  3. notes that the reasons for Council’s decision that a satisfactory result would not be achieved by inviting tenders for the Proposed Contract are that:
    1. previous tenders connected with the project have not produced satisfactory tender responses in respect of the Proposed Contract; and
    2. inviting tenders in respect of the Proposed Contract will unduly delay the project and likely increase risk to Council and increase project costs through delay, as further described in the Confidential Report;
  4. authorises the General Manager to:
    1. directly negotiate with the contractor identified as the preferred contractor in the Confidential Report (Preferred Contractor) for the purposes of entering into the Proposed Contract; and
    2. execute any agreement arising from those direct negotiations; and
  5. if an agreement is executed as a result of the negotiations authorised under paragraph 4, resolves to novate the contract between Council and Wilde Civil Pty Ltd ACN 108 593 808 (Wilde Civil) in relation to the Moree Artesian Aquatic Centre Redevelopment Stage 1A, to the Preferred Contractor, and authorises the General Manager to:
    1. directly negotiate with the Preferred Contractor and Wilde Civil for the purposes of entering into a deed of novation; and
    2. execute any deed arising from those direct negotiations.

Against: Cr James

In accordance with the Local Government Act 1993 and the Local Government (General) Regulation 2021, in the opinion of the General Manager, the following business is of a kind as referred to in Section 10A(2) of the Act, and should be dealt with in a part of the meeting closed to the media and public. 

(a)      personnel matters concerning particular individuals (other than councillors),

1.    That Council move into closed council to consider business identified, tabled at the meeting.

2.    That pursuant under Section 10A(1)-(3) of the Local Government Act 1993, the media and public be excluded from the meeting on the basis that the business to be considered is classified confidential under the provisions of Section 10A(2) as outlined above.

3.    That the correspondence and reports relevant to the subject business be withheld from access to the media and public as required by Section 11(2) of the Local Government Act 1993.
The Council moved into closed Council at the time being 11.02am. The public and staff left the meeting and media left the Chamber. Mr Tytherleigh left the meeting declaring an interest. Ms Murray and Mr Baldwin remained in the meeting. 
2024/12/45 RESOLVED (MOVED: Councillor Pearse / SECONDED: Councillor Sauer)

(a) Amends the term of the office of the Mayor from 15 October 2024 up to and including 12 December 2024.
(b) Notes that this motion would declare the position of Mayor as vacant. 
The Motion upon being PUT was declared LOST. 
Division Vote; 

For: Cr James. 
Against: Crs Sauer, Mailler, Williams, Tighe, Hodgkinson and Cassells.

That council notes the resignation of Mr Kelvin Tytherleigh and thanks him for his service to the Moree Plains Shire, including the below significant achievements:
  • Advocacy of our shire and region with other local, state and federal governments including on Inland Rail, the Moree Special Activation Precinct, and crime and community safety, including award winning collaboration with Balonne Shire Council on cross-border initiatives;
  • Development and implementation of the award winning Burnt and Derelict Housing Program, resulting in 40 properties being remediated since February 2024;
  • Upgrades to airport infrastructure enabling improved service for our Regular Passenger Transport with QantasLink;
  • Progression of key strategic projects including the Moree Artesian Aquatic Centre; and 
  • Support of our team, improving workplace culture and practices.
Cr Tighe addressed the Chambers to reiterate the Mayor's sentiment.

That Council:
  1. notes Report 19.2 “Confidential - Moree Artesian Aquatic Centre Redevelopment _ Contract 3” presented at the Ordinary Council Meeting of 12 December 2024 (Confidential Report);
  2. resolves that because of extenuating circumstances and the unavailability of competitive or reliable tenderers, a satisfactory result would not be achieved by inviting tenders for the engagement of a head contractor for the Moree Artesian Aquatic Centre Redevelopment (Proposed Contract);
  3. notes that the reasons for Council’s decision that a satisfactory result would not be achieved by inviting tenders for the Proposed Contract are that:
    1. previous tenders connected with the project have not produced satisfactory tender responses in respect of the Proposed Contract; and
    2. inviting tenders in respect of the Proposed Contract will unduly delay the project and likely increase risk to Council and increase project costs through delay, as further described in the Confidential Report;
  4. authorises the General Manager to:
    1. directly negotiate with the contractor identified as the preferred contractor in the Confidential Report (Preferred Contractor) for the purposes of entering into the Proposed Contract; and
    2. execute any agreement arising from those direct negotiations; and
  5. if an agreement is executed as a result of the negotiations authorised under paragraph 4, resolves to novate the contract between Council and Wilde Civil Pty Ltd ACN 108 593 808 (Wilde Civil) in relation to the Moree Artesian Aquatic Centre Redevelopment Stage 1A, to the Preferred Contractor, and authorises the General Manager to:
    1. directly negotiate with the Preferred Contractor and Wilde Civil for the purposes of entering into a deed of novation; and
    2. execute any deed arising from those direct negotiations.

 18.1 Confidential - Mungindi Junior Rugby League Clubhouse - Project Update
 
 That Council:

1. That following advice from the Interim General Manager, Council endorses the following projects funded under the Local Roads and Community Infrastructure Program:

That Council:
1. Nominate the Mayor, Councillor Hodgkinson and the Interim General Manager to attend the 2025 National General Assembly of Local Government (NGA) incorporating the Regional Cooperation and Development Forum to be held at the National Convention Centre, Canberra from Tuesday 24 June 2025 to Friday 27 June 2025. 

2. Put forward the following motions at the 2025 NGA:
a. That the Federal Government considers shifting the road network funding model of the Financial Assistance Grant from a population based allocation to a model based on the total length of the road network kilometres within the LGA.
b. That the Federal Government recognises the strategic National importance of increase investment in regional infrastructure to support local industry, jobs and regional economic and population growth, funding it accordingly.
c. That the Federal Government take an urgent and proactive action to provide an equitable level of services in communication and connectivity across all of Australia.

3. Endorse Councillor Hodgkinson as the second Council representative along with the Mayor at the 2025 NGA to move and speak to Council's motions, if required.

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"2025/6/7  RESOLVED (MOVED: Councillor Sauer / SECONDED: Councillor Tighe)
That Council, pursuant to Section 535 of the Local Government Act 1993 (the Act), make the following rates and charges for the 2025/2026 rating period:

1. Make the General Rates
In accordance with Section 494 of the Local Government Act 1993, Council make and levy the following ordinary rates for the year 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2026, 

a) Make a Residential Rate 
Residential Ad Valorem rate (to apply to rateable land categorised as Residential within Moree Plains Shire in accordance with Section 516 of the Act) of 0.01080344 cents in the dollar and having a base rate of $500 per assessment (representing 17.15% of the total yield in accordance with Section 500 of the Act), yielding a total income of $4,849,011 in compliance with Council's allowable Notional Income.
   
b) Make a Residential Rural Rate 
Residential Rural Ad Valorem rate (to apply to all rateable land Sub-categorised Residential Rural within Moree Plains Shire in accordance with Section 529 (2)(b) of the Act) of 0.01080344 cents in the dollar and having a base rate of $500 per assessment (representing 2.75% of the total yield in accordance with Section 500 of the Act), yielding a total income of $777,610 in compliance with Council's allowable Notional Income.

c) Make a Business Moree Rate
Business Moree Ad Valorem rate (to apply to all rateable land sub-categorised Business Moree within Moree Plains Shire in accordance with Section 529(2)(d) of the Act) of 0.03474182 cents in the dollar and having a base rate of $500 (representing 11.13% of the total yield in accordance with Section 500 of the Act), yielding a total income of $3,146,602 in compliance with Council’s allowable Notional Income.   

d) Make a Business Rate 
Business Ad Valorem rate (to apply to all rateable land categorised Business within Moree Plains Shire in accordance with Section 518 of the Act) of 0.00812366 cents in the dollar and having a base rate of $500 (representing 0.66% of the total income in accordance with Section 500 of the Act), yielding a total income of $185,612 in compliance with Council's allowable Notional Income. 

e) Make a Farmland Rate 
Farmland Ad Valorem rate (to apply to all rateable land categorised as Farmland within Moree Plains Shire in accordance with Section 515 of the Act) of 0.00160795 cents in the dollar and having a base rate of $500 per assessment (representing 66.75% of the total yield in accordance with Section 500 of the Act), yielding a total income of $18,879,300 in compliance with Council's Allowable Notional Income.

f) Make a Mining Rate
Mining Ad Valorem rate (to apply to all rateable land categorised as Mining within Moree Plains Shire in accordance with Section 515) of 2.87370000 cents in the dollar and having a base rate of $20,000 per assessment (representing 0% of the total yield in accordance with Section 500 of the Act), yielding a total income of $0 in compliance with Council's Allowable Notional Income

Make a Special Rate
g) Make a Business Intensive Ginning/Receival Centre – Special Rate 
Business Intensive Ginning/Receival Centre Ad Valorem rate (to apply to all rateable land Sub-categorised Business Intensive Ginning/Receival Centre within Moree Plains Shire in accordance with Section 529(2)(d) of the Act) of 0.03368739 cents in the dollar and having a base rate of $1,360 per assessment (representing 1.56% of the total yield in accordance with Section 500 of the Act), yielding a total income of $441,783 in compliance with Council's allowable Notional Income.  

2. Make a Water Charge
In relation to water supply charges; in accordance with Section 501 and Section 502 of the Local Government Act 1993, Council make and levy the following charges for Water Supply Services in 2025/2026:
Make an Availability Charge:

  1. Charge each parcel of separately valued land one availability charge per annum of $283.33 for each Council connected water meter for residential customers that have a 20mm, 25mm or 32mm connection. 
  2. Charge vacant land without a water meter an availability charge is $141.94 (which is 50% of the current residential availability charge). Residents with a larger connection will pay an access charge based on the following non-residual charges.
  3. Non-Residential Water Availability Charge 20mm connection $283.88
  4. Non-Residential Water Availability Charge 25mm connection $443.56
  5. Non-Residential Water Availability Charge 32mm connection $726.73
  6. Residential and Non-Residential Water Availability Charge 40mm connection $1,135.51
  7. Residential and Non-Residential Water Availability Charge 50mm connection $1,774.23
  8. Residential and Non-Residential Water Availability Charge 80mm connection $4,542.03
  9. Residential and Non-Residential Water Availability Charge 100mm connection $7,096.93
  10. Residential and Non-Residential Water Availability Charge 150mm connection $15,968.08
  11. Residential and Non-Residential Water Availability Charge 200mm connection $28,387.70

Make a Water Consumption Charge
In relation to water consumption charges; pursuant to Section 502 of the Local Government Act make the following charges for 2025/2026
 
a. Potable Water Consumption Charge of $1.89 per KL up to 750 KL per annum (known as tier 1)
b. Potable Water Consumption Charge of $2.77 per KL above 750 KL per annum (known as tier 2
c. Non-Potable Water Consumption Charge of $1.26 per KL up to 750 KL per annum (known as tier 1)
d. Non-Potable Water Consumption Charge of $1.85 per KL above 750 KL per annum (known as tier 2)

3. Make a Sewer Charge
In relation to sewerage service charges; in accordance with Section 501 and Section 502 of the Local Government Act 1993, Council make and levy the charges for Sewerage Services in 2025/2026 as follows:
  1. Residential sewer charges will consist of one flat tariff of $877.61
  2. All non-residential properties will be charged based on a two-tier pricing system. Sewer charges will be in accordance with Best Practice Pricing guidelines, which prescribes an availability charge based upon the corresponding water meter connection size. The Sewerage Discharge Factor is charged at a per kilolitre usage charges of $1.59 per KL based on water usage and disposal estimates.
  3. Non-Residential Sewer Availability based on water connection 20mm $720.09
  4. Non-Residential Sewer Availability based on water connection 25mm $877.61
  5. Non-Residential Sewer Availability based on water connection 32mm $1,437.88
  6. Non-Residential Sewer Availability based on water connection 40mm $2,246.69
  7. Non-Residential Sewer Availability based on water connection 50mm $3,510.45
  8. Non-Residential Sewer Availability based on water connection 80mm $8,986.74
  9. Non-Residential Sewer Availability based on water connection 100mm $14,041.79
  10. Non-Residential Sewer Availability based on water connection 150mm $31,594.03
  11. Non-Residential Sewer Availability based on water connection 200mm $56,167.16
  12. Non-Residential No Water Connection $877.61
  13. Sewer Balone Shire $2,633.51
  14. Gurley Common Effluent Charge $614.33
 
4. Make a Waste Charge
 
In relation to waste management charges, in accordance with Section 496 and Section 501 and Section 502 of the Local Government Act 1993, Council make and levy the annual charges for Waste Management Services in 2025/2026 as follows:
 
  1. All residential properties containing a single dwelling or strata unit/flat within the collection service areas will be levied a “Domestic Waste Management Charge”, where the service is available. This charge per annum is $420.77 for a 140lt bin.
  2. Vacant waste charge is applicable for each parcel of valued vacant rateable land for which the service is available and is $105.19 (based on 25% of the Domestic Waste Collection).
  3. Additional Domestic Waste Services are as follows:
    1. Upgrade - Domestic Large Bin (240L) $91.53
    2. Upgrade - Recycle Bin (360L) $24.38
    3. Additional Service - Organic Bin (240L) $24.38
    4. Additional Service - Recycle Bin (240L) $109.78
    5. Additional Service - Recycle Bin (360L) $134.21
  4. Properties containing a place of business or industry or where activity other than private residential occupation occurs (excepting caravan and mobile home parks), including properties exempt from the levy of the Ordinary Rate, and who avail themselves of Council’s collection service are charged a Commercial Waste Management Charge of $277.71.
  5. Additional Non-Domestic Waste services are as follows:
    1. Additional Service - Waste (240L) $186.60
    2. Upgrade - Recycle Bin (360L) $24.38
    3. Request Organic Bin (240L) $24.38
  6. Waste Management Levy – Urban $339.02
  7. Waste Management Levy – Rural $169.51
 
5. Make an Interest Charge
 
In accordance with section 566(3) of the Act, it has been determined that the maximum rate of interest payable on overdue rates and charges for the period 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2026 (inclusive) will be 10.5% per annum

That Council:
  1. Note the report for information.
  2. Proceed with Scenario 1, as described in the Report, which awaits a determination from Heritage NSW regarding Council's request for review of the Taylor Oval Site Listing based on evidence detailed on the Site Card. 
  3. If Heritage NSW's approves Council's request, bring a Report back to Council to consider the 50m concept options for construction and to seek Council's endorsement for undertaking grant funding variations requests to complete the project.
  4. If Heritage NSW's denies Council's request, delegate to the General Manager to proceed with Scenario 2, as described in the Report, and fund this body of work from the MAAC Reconstruction/Refurbishment Project and endorse the undertaking of grant funding variation requests to complete the project, subject to an affirmative resolution of the Scenario 2 investigative actions.
  5. Note that if Scenario 2 is commenced, the investigative work is expected to take at least 40 weeks during which period of time there will be no construction occurring at Taylor Oval. Also, note that the investigation does not guarantee that the necessary clearance would be achieved from Heritage NSW to commence construction at Taylor Oval after the investigation has been completed.

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":" 2025/8/12  RESOLVED (MOVED: Councillor McGrady / SECONDED: Councillor James)

That:
Council investigate the feasibility of constructing two helipads for Toomelah and Boggabilla, to address issues that arise when these two communities become isolated during a flood event and ambulances cannot access people needing urgent medical assistance.

I present the following justification for this NoM:
1. The isolation and lack of professionals residing in these communities.
2. Resident medical professionals only visit these communities during business hours.
3. Both communities become isolated during flood events.
4. Both communities have been evacuated due to flooding over the past 5 years.
5. Both communities have ample vacant land to accommodate a helipad (x2).
6. The Toomelah community don't have  after hours access to quality health advice after community health workers   
    leave after 5pm M-F.
7. Very ill and infirmed residents have had to have their medication air dropped during previous flood events. This also 
    raises concerns as to how the very ill would be evacuated safely during a flood when the community is isolated and  
   Toomelah becomes an island surrounded by the McIntyre River, Dumaresq River and Whalan Creek.

The CEO of the Toomelah LALC has given full support to this proposal.

This project is not funded or resourced under Council's current Operational Plan.  The project can be "taken under notice" for consideration in 2026/27.

22.4 Confidential Code of Conduct – Special Complaint Handling Agreement

That Council:
 
  1.
