22.7 Confidential – Audit Risk Improvement Committee Chairperson

That Council appoints Applicant A to the role of Chair of the Audit Risk and Improvement Committee, as per the Attached resume.  
 

22.2 Confidential - Expression of Interest to Purchase Lots 1 and 2 Section 27 DP 758729, known as 30 Mugul Street, Mungindi

That Council:
  1. Approve the sale of Lots 1 and 2 Section 27 DP 758729, known as 30 Mogul Street Mungindi by the process of direct negotiation with Landify Pty Ltd (ACN 638 868 970) or associated entity.
  2. Delegate to the General Manager to negotiate a sale price in line with "Confidential Note", included in this report, in respect of 30 Mogul Street Mungindi.
  3. That all documents associated with the sale between Moree Plains Shire Council and Landify Pty Ltd (ACN 638 868 970) or associated entity be executed under Council seal.


22.3 Expression of Interest to Purchase Lot 159 DP 748657, known as Lot 159 Wilga Place, Moree

That Council: 
  1. Offer for sale of Lot 159 DP 748657, known as Lot 159 Wilga Place, Moree by the process of direct negotiation with Abcare, provided Abcare is successful in securing funding under the NSW Government’s Aboriginal Child and Family Centre (ACFC) Expansion Program (Round 2), which closes on 1 August 2025. 
  2. Delegate to the General Manager to negotiate a sale price, in line with Confidential Note, in respect of Lot 159 Wilga Place, Moree.
  3. Issue a letter of commitment to sell Lot 159 Wilga Place, Moree at the agreed sale price, subject to Abcare's success with the ACFC Expansion Program (Round 2) Tender. 
  4. That all documents associated with the sale between Moree Plains Shire Council and Abcare, or associated entity, be executed under Council seal.


22.5 Confidential - Sale of Land for Unpaid Rates – Update

That Council delegates to the General Manager the authority to negotiate the sale and accept any offer deemed reasonable in respect to the level of outstanding debts and saleability of the properties listed in the confidential report.


22.6 Expression of Interest to Purchase Boomi Airstrip being Lot 2 DP 528906, known as 7993 Carrigan Road, Boomi

  1. Offer for sale Lot 2 DP 528906, known as 7993 Carrigan Road, Boomi by the process of direct negotiation. 
  2. Delegate to the General Manager to negotiate a sale price, in line with the Confidential Note 1, in respect of 7993 Carrigan Road Boomi. 
  3. That all documents associated with the sale of the land be executed under Council seal.
 

22.8 Organisational Structure
That Council:
1. Endorse the organisation structure in accordance with Diagram 2 within the report.
2. Receive a further report at the 18th September Ordinary Council Meeting following the General Manager's consultation with staff. Strategic Review and Asset Management Improvement Plan for Roads

BACKGROUND
We are now one year into the 2024-2028 councillor term. During the election, candidates heard repeatedly that roads were a major concern for the community and 12 months later, they remain the biggest issue that affects the full geography of our shire which council has direct responsibility for. 
The current state of the roads has come about through many reasons with floods, wet seasons, delays in funding, policy decisions, procurement issues, a long term lack of strategic asset management planning and volatility in our internal resourcing all contributing. 
We are now about to embark on what is likely to be one of our region’s most productive winter cropping harvests, with a road network broadly unable to depended on. This is not a position our council wants to be in and hence it is time for a strategic re-think in terms of how council maintains, sustains, improves and funds our road network. 
With our Road Network Advisory Committee now back in action, it is the right time to be embarking on a strategic review of council’s roads service provision, working with our producers, councillors, and building upon learnings of our and other shires to develop a clear and long-term plan for improvement.  
A Roads Asset Management Plan is a requirement under the Office of Local Government’s Integrated Planning and Reporting Framework. Our council has however been without this document - which is supposed to directly inform our Delivery Program, Operational Plan and Budget, and Long Term Financial Plan - for some time. 
We have an opportunity to not only cover the minimum required standard, but also undertake a comprehensive rethink, setting up our council and team to better manage the road task. 
In addition, Council adopted an updated Self Help Program Policy in July 2025, which has since had a number of applications from road users to assist with that task. The applications however have not been reviewed or approved. These applications which seek to add value to roads, augmenting council funding and works, and reducing road user risk, need to be dealt with swiftly.  "},{"id":919,"motionedByName":null,"secondedByName":null,"motionAction":null,"voteForNames":null,"voteAgainstNames":null,"voteAbstainNames":null,"voteResult":null,"motionText":"

  2025/10/15  RESOLVED (MOVED: Councillor Cassells / SECONDED: Councillor Hodgkinson)

That Council: 
1. Note that the Moree Cultural Art Foundation Funding Agreement remains unexecuted due to incomplete and unreconciled asset-register schedules provided by Bank Art Museum Moree (BAMM) that differ significantly from the Council-adopted asset-register schedules from 2021 (attached). 

2. Consider a further report once a reconciliation is provided by BAMM between the 2021 Council-adopted asset register and the 2025 asset register with any discrepancies formally resolved and explained by BAMM.
3. Seek confirmation from BAMM that no changes to asset ownership will be made without formal Council approval.

The General Manager read out the following in open Council:

Report:  22.1 Engagement of Project Management Services for Flood Recovery Works under AGRN 1119 & 1034
 
RESOLVED (MOVED: Councillor Tighe / SECONDED: Councillor Cassells)
 
 That Council:
  1. Accepts the NSW Public Works offer for provision of Project Managment Services for Essential Public Asset Repair works for events AGRN 1119 & 1034 
  2. Delegates to the General Manager the authority to approve all purchasing activities necessary for the undertaking of the recommended engagement


 
Report: 22.3 CONFIDENTIAL – RFQ-2005519 Bridge Works Design – Flood Recovery
 
RESOLVED (MOVED: Councillor Sauer / SECONDED: Councillor Tighe)
 
 That Council:
  1. Note that Public Works NSW conducted the procurement process for RFQ-2005519 – MPSC Bridge Works Design Consultancy in accordance with the Local Government (General) Regulation 2021, ensuring fairness, transparency, and competition.
  2. Acknowledge that all quotations received exceeded the $250,000 tender threshold due to the dispersed nature of the project scope and the current market demand for specialist bridge-design consultancy services.
  3. Resolve, in accordance with Section 55(3)(i) of the Local Government Act 1993 and Clause 178(3)(e) of the Local Government (General) Regulation 2021, that there are extenuating circumstances relating to the urgent timing of the flood-recovery bridge-design works, and that it is in the public interest not to invite further tenders.
  4. Accept the quotation from the Recommended Supplier for the provision of bridge-design consultancy services under RFQ-2005519 for the amount set out in the report.
  5. Delegate authority to the General Manager to:
     a. Finalise contract terms with the Recommended Supplier; and
     b. Execute all necessary documentation to engage Recommended Supplier and proceed with the delivery of the design works.
  6. Note that project costs remain within the approved upper limit of the Essential Public Asset Restoration (EPAR) Agreement when existing contingencies are applied, and that Council will seek a variation from the NSW Reconstruction Authority to increase the approved upper limit to reinstate contingencies for the construction phase.
 
Report: 21.1 CONFIDENTIAL – Audit Risk Improvement Committee Chairperson and Members
 
 RESOLVED (MOVED: Councillor Sauer / SECONDED: Councillor Hodgkinson)
 
 That Council: 
 1. Appoints Applicant A as the Chairperson of the ARIC for a two-year term, with an option for an additional two-year extension.
2. Appoints Applicants B and C as Independent Members of the ARIC for a two-year term, with an option for an additional two-year extension.



There being no further business the meeting closed, the time being 04:56PM

Motion subject

Motion

National Objective

Motion Subject
Crime
Motion
Call on the NSW Government to:
    1. Further strengthen the Bail Act to drastrically reduce or eliminate the number of repeat offenders with a history of serious or violent crimes being granted bail;
    2. Reverse the onus on doli incapax; 
    3. Amend the Crimes (sentencing procedure) Act to elevate the importance of the impact of the crime on the victim at the point of sentencing.
    4. And a suggestion- something against the centralisation of court/AVL bail hearings in Parramatta Children's Court and Parramatta Bail Court - some context here: Bail Centralisation and the Virtual Bail Court: NSW Staggers into a Reform Overreach 
National Objective

Summary of key arguments


Motion Subject
Arts Funding
Motion
Call on the NSW Government to:
  • Restore arts funding to rural and regional areas.     
National Objective

Summary of key arguments
Context: BAMM routinely received funding from Create NSW, however they - and other rural and regional galleries - have not received this funding for the first time in years, reducing service provision in rural and regional NSW and increasing cost shifting to local government and disadvantaged communities. We could get more info from Rosie at BAMM if councillors wished to support a motion like this.

Motion Subject
Virtual Care
Motion

  • Provide councils with quarterly reporting on the frequency of use of Virtual Care in rural and regional Emergency Departments;
  • Directly employ Emergency Department doctors in rural emergency departments (I can pull together some better wording)
National Objective
Virtual Care must only be the backup care not the primary.
Summary of arguments

 


Motion Subject
Roads
Motion
Addressing the fundamental  funding issues for regional road networks
National Objective
Summary of key arguments

That Council note:
  1. The update on the progress in developing the Integrated Water Cycle Management Strategy 
  2. The Water & Sewerage Strategy - Scenario Analysis Report and that
    1. All water supply scenarios for the town of Moree require use of Great Artesian Basin (GAB) water to provide adequate supply for the adopted SAP and Housing development scenarios of between 10% and 30%
    2. The potential raw water supply scenarios for the Lower Gwydir aquifer are currently being confirmed for extraction capacity and feasibility to finalise the identification of the preferred supply scenario and hence GAB volume requirements
    3. All water supply scenarios are based on achieving the modelled water demand reduction of 228 Ml/year including leakage reduction and dwelling retrofit opportunities at ultimate development in year 2052
  3. That a presentation and workshop on the Water & Sewerage Scenario Analysis Report will be conducted by NSW Public Works in February 2026 with the draft Integrated Water Cycle Management Strategy scheduled to be reported to Council in February 2026

That Council:
1.      Note that the ownership allocation discrepancies identified by Council in October 2025 in the Moree Cultural and Art Foundation Ltd (ABN 87 003 435 765) (the Foundation) schedule have been corrected by the Foundation;
2.      Note that a stocktake has been performed on Council’s assets and that this process identified unsighted assets which require follow-up with the Foundation;
3.      Note that the Foundation has advised it no longer operates as a ‘Keeping Place’ for Aboriginal stones and artefacts;
4.      Decline the request to transfer four artworks, recorded as Council-owned in schedule 1 of the Funding Agreement dated 14 October 2021 (the 2021 Funding Agreement), to become assets of the Foundation; subject to further information from the donor and seeking legal advise; 
5.      Note its intention to maintain ownership of all artworks, artefacts and assets recorded as Council-owned in schedules 1 and 2 of the 2021 Funding Agreement to be carried through to the 2025 Funding Agreement;
6.      Approve an interim payment of $100,000 to the Foundation for the continued provision of services listed in the 2021 Funding Agreement; and
7.      That Council amend the proposed 2025 Funding Agreement with the Foundation to include provisions to address concerns related to the control, management, maintenance and auditing of Councils assets and the Foundations compliance with contractual obligations. 

Not Present: Councillors Tighe and Williams

Cr Wayne Tighe returned to the meeting the time being 03:43pm.

 
2025/12/20  RESOLVED (MOVED: Councillor Cassells / SECONDED: Councillor Sauer)

That there be a short break in the meeting.
The break in the meeting began at the time being 03:43pm and resumed the time being 04:03pm.

That Council note: 
  1. That Council is engaging with the Regional Growth NSW Development Corporation (RGDC) regarding the negotiation of the Deed for the Moree Special Activation Precinct Master Plan; 
  1. That Council is negotiating with RGDC on the successful implementation of the Deed to ensure that capital assets transferred for public benefit meet community expectations and are fit for purpose, that the agreement represents a reasonable balancing of commercial risk, and that assets are acquired at a financial value that does not pose an unreasonable risk or impact on Council’s budget.
  2. That RGDC is projecting that the capital value of transferred Special Activation Precinct assets to Council is $79M, which will lead to approximately $1.4M of additional annual depreciation for Council.
  3. That NSW Public Works project that Council needs to invest in Water Fund capital upgrade expenditure of approximately $65M and Sewer Fund capital upgrade expenditure of $27M in the next 30 years but starting from year 5 to, also, cater for the needs of the Special Activation Precinct.
  4. That the impact of all of the above will render the General Fund financially unsustainable and this will most likely necessitate a special rate variation.
  5. That the impact of the Water Fund will likely lead to further water fee increases.
  6. The General Manager arrange a workshop between Council, Councillors and RGDC for a full debrief on the Special Activation Precinct in February 2026

  1. Note that Council is engaging with the Regional Growth NSW Development Corporation regarding the negotiation of the Deed for the Moree Special Activation Precinct Master Plan; 
  1. Endorse a staged delivery approach for the Moree Plains Special Activation Precinct infrastructure.

RESOLVED (MOVED: Councillor Cassells / SECONDED: Councillor Sauer)
 
 That Council:
  1. Note the report regarding the status of the existing Companion Animal Management Facility, including the operational limitations of the current pound and the partially constructed building associated with DA 2017/83, including that completion of the building in its current form is not recommended.
  2. Receive and note the Preliminary Cost Plan prepared by MCG Quantity Surveyors ACN 150 345 654, provided as a Confidential Attachment.

In accordance with the Local Government Act 1993 and the Local Government (General) Regulation 2021, in the opinion of the General Manager, the following business is of a kind as referred to in Section 10A(2) of the Act, and should be dealt with in a part of the meeting closed to the media and public. 

23.6 Taylor Oval Aquatic Precinct - update

(a)   personnel matters concerning particular individuals (other than councillors),
(b)   the personal hardship of any resident or ratepayer,
(c)   information that would, if disclosed, confer a commercial advantage on a person with whom the council is conducting (or proposes to conduct) business,
(d)   commercial information of a confidential nature that would, if disclosed:
(i)       prejudice the commercial position of the person who supplied it, or
(ii)      confer a commercial advantage on a competitor of the council, or 
(iii)     reveal a trade secret,
(e)   information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law,
(f)   matters affecting the security of the council, councillors, council staff or council property,
(g)   advice concerning litigation, or advice that would otherwise be privileged from production in legal proceedings on the ground of legal professional privilege,
(h)   information concerning the nature and location of a place or an item of Aboriginal significance on community land,
(i)   alleged contraventions of any code of conduct requirements applicable under section 440.

1.    That Council move into closed council to consider business identified, tabled at the meeting.

2. That pursuant under Section 10A(1)-(3) of the Local Government Act 1993, the media and public be excluded from the meeting on the basis that the business to be considered is classified confidential under the provisions of Section 10A(2) as outlined above.

3. That the correspondence and reports relevant to the subject business be withheld from access to the media and public as required by Section 11(2) of the Local Government Act 1993.

The Council moved into closed Council at the time being 02:57pm. The public and media left the Chamber.
FOR: Susannah Pearse, Brooke Sauer, Peter Mailler, Debra Williams, Frederick McGrady, Wayne Tighe, Kelly James, Kerry Cassells  
AGAINST: None

That Council:
  1. Note the updated advice from Heritage NSW regarding the AHIMS site listing for Taylor Oval and the appointment of an archaeological consultant to undertake the required Aboriginal cultural heritage assessment and AHIP process.

[IGNORE_INDENT]","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"2026/5/6 RESOLVED (MOVED: Councillor Pearse / SECONDED: Councillor Tighe)

That Council:
  1. notes the release of the LGNSW’s “Caring for our Regions” Six Point Action Plan on Rural and Regional Health, which outlines coordinated advocacy priorities to address critical gaps in healthcare access and outcomes for rural, regional and remote communities;
  2. recognises that people living in rural, regional and remote areas experience poorer health outcomes, reduced access to primary and specialist care, and shorter life expectancy compared to metropolitan communities, and that these inequities are unacceptable;
  3. adopts the “Caring for our Regions” Action Plan on Rural and Regional Health as a formal advocacy position of Council;
  4. undertakes appropriate media and communications opportunities to publicly support the “Caring for our Regions” Action Plan on Rural and Regional Health and strengthen coordinated advocacy with other councils.
  5. writes to the NSW Minister for Regional Health, Ryan Park MP; the Commonwealth Assistant Minister for Rural and Regional Health, Emma McBride MP; and the local Member(s) of Parliament (State and Commonwealth), seeking their support for the “Caring for our Regions”  Action Plan on Rural and Regional Health and calling for coordinated State and Commonwealth action to improve rural and regional health outcomes.
  6. notify LGNSW of this notice of motion.

FOR: Susannah Pearse, Peter Mailler, Debra Williams, Frederick McGrady, Wayne Tighe, Dominique Hodgkinson, Kerry Cassells  
AGAINST: None
ABSTAIN: None
ABSENT:  Brooke Sauer, Kelly James

That council:
  1. Acknowledges the receipt of the General Manager's resignation, effective 18 June 2026;
  2. Offers its heartfelt thanks to Ms Cowley for her service to the shire, including leading the organisation and our team to deliver:
    1. Completion of the long-awaited Moree Memorial Hall (closed since 2019), the hot artesian pools at the Moree Artesian Aquatic Centre (active pool closed since 2022), a raft of projects on-deadline and at risk of grant funding loss under the Local Roads and Community Infrastructure Program, and significant progress on the Ron Harborne Precinct;
    2. Improved financial sustainability, including improving financial discipline throughout the organisation, restoring unrestricted cash, and improving the health of the water fund;
    3. New standards for the organisation including implementing new corporate values to improve customer service, value for ratepayer money, and the functioning of the organisation; and
    4. Strong leadership and a legacy that will last for future generations.

FOR: Susannah Pearse, Peter Mailler, Debra Williams, Frederick McGrady, Wayne Tighe, Dominique Hodgkinson, Kerry Cassells  
AGAINST: None
ABSTAIN: None
ABSENT:  Brooke Sauer, Kelly James

Carried 


2026/5/8 RESOLVED (MOVED: Councillor Pearse / SECONDED: Councillor Tighe)

 That Council
1. In accordance with the NSW Office of Local Government's Guidelines for the Appointment and Oversight of the General Manager (2022, p.7), delegates to the Mayor to:
  1. commence an Expression of Interest (EOI) process for an external recruitment consultant to lead the application process for the position of General Manager;
  1. Ensure the General Manager's position description is current and evaluated in terms of salary to reflect the responsibilities of the position;
  1. Ensure the position is advertised in accordance with the requirements of the Act;
  1. Establish a Selection Panel led by the Mayor, and including the Deputy Mayor, Councillor Williams, and the recruiter as the independent member to shortlist applications (noting interviews will be conducted by the full council); 
  1. In consultation with Council representatives on the Selection Panel, appoint the recruiter.

Council resolves:
1. That pursuant to clause 7.37(b) of the Procedures for the Administration of the Model Code of Conduct for Local Councils in New South Wales (Procedures) and section 440G of the Local Government Act 1993, Council formally censure Councillor Kelly James on the grounds that the Councillor's conduct, during the course of the Extraordinary Council Meeting of 5 February 2026, has been found by an independent investigator to constitute a breach of the following provisions of Council's Code of Conduct:
  1. 3.1(a) - conducting herself in a manner that is likely to bring the Council or other council officials into disrepute; and
  2. 3.1(b) - conduct contrary to statutory requirements or the council’s administrative requirements or policies; and
  3. 3.21 - conduct that disrupts council or committee meetings or would otherwise be inconsistent with the orderly conduct of meetings; and
  4. 3.22 - acts of disorder or other conduct at council meetings that are intended to prevent the proper or effective functioning of the council.
2. That pursuant to clause 7.39 of the Procedures, Council revise its Code of Meeting Practice concerning audio visual link (AVL) attendance at Ordinary and Extraordinary meetings of Council by councillors to ensure that:
  1. Physical attendance at Ordinary or Extraordinary meetings of Council would be the preferred mode of attendance by councillors and accordingly, attendance by AVL should be limited to truly exceptional circumstances and not become an established pattern for any councillor; and
  2. A councillor must not make their AVL from a motor vehicle or other external location from which privacy or the councillor’s full attention to the meeting cannot be guaranteed.
3. Delegates to the General Manager to issue a statement advising the community of this censure, noting that Cr James was censured for similar misconduct on 18 July 2024.
4. Delegates to the General Manager to implement the suggested revisions to the Code of Meeting Practice.

FOR: Susannah Pearse, Peter Mailler, Debra Williams, Wayne Tighe, Dominique Hodgkinson, Kerry Cassells

The General Manager read aloud in open Council:


Report 22.1 CONFIDENTIAL - Sale of Lot 35 DP 1261087 (Gateway South) to Mataso Spec Pty Ltd (ACN: 619 400 789)

That Council:

  1. Provides Mataso Spec Pty Ltd (ACN: 619 400 789) with notice to rescind the contract for sale of Lot 35 DP 1261087, dated 23 April 2019.
  2. Delegates to the General Manager authority to negotiate a new contract of sale with Mataso Spec Pty Ltd (ACN: 619 400 789) for Lot 35 DP 1261087.
  3. Remains committed to a sale with amended and updated contract conditions. 


 

Report 22.2 Delegation to the General Manager - Moree Regional Airport Runway Rehabilitation

That the Council delegate to the General Manager the acceptance of the pavement repair quotes and the expenditure of up to $1,450,000 for rehabilitation works to runway 01/19 at the Moree Regional Airport.



Report 22.4 Confidential Report - Ron Harborne Oval Netball Precinct Construction - Contractor Engagement

That Council:

  1. Pursuant to section 55(3)(i) of the Local Government Act 1993, resolves not to invite tenders, due to extenuating circumstances associated with grant funding expiry on 30 June 2026.
  2. Accept the quotation from NJ Cobb Construction PTY LTD (ABN 58 681 429 121).
  3. Delegate authority under section 377 of the Local Government Act to the General Manager to execute the contract documents.


Report 22.3 Confidential - Code of Conduct Breach - Consideration of Final Investigation Report

Council resolves:
 1. That pursuant to clause 7.37(b) of the Procedures for the Administration of the Model Code of Conduct for Local Councils in New South Wales (Procedures) and section 440G of the Local Government Act 1993, Council formally censure Councillor Kelly James on the grounds that the Councillor's conduct, during the course of the Extraordinary Council Meeting of 5 February 2026, has been found by an independent investigator to constitute a breach of the following provisions of Council's Code of Conduct:

  1. 3.1(a) - conducting herself in a manner that is likely to bring the Council or other council officials into disrepute; and
  2. 3.1(b) - conduct contrary to statutory requirements or the council’s administrative requirements or policies; and
  3. 3.21 - conduct that disrupts council or committee meetings or would otherwise be inconsistent with the orderly conduct of meetings; and
  4. 3.22 - acts of disorder or other conduct at council meetings that are intended to prevent the proper or effective functioning of the council.

2. That pursuant to clause 7.39 of the Procedures, Council revise its Code of Meeting Practice concerning audio visual link (AVL) attendance at Ordinary and Extraordinary meetings of Council by councillors to ensure that:

  1. Physical attendance at Ordinary or Extraordinary meetings of Council would be the preferred mode of attendance by councillors and accordingly, attendance by AVL should be limited to truly exceptional circumstances and not become an established pattern for any councillor; and
  2. A councillor must not make their AVL from a motor vehicle or other external location from which privacy or the councillor’s full attention to the meeting cannot be guaranteed.

3. Delegates to the General Manager to issue a statement advising the community of this censure, noting that Cr James was censured for similar misconduct on 18 July 2024.


 4. Delegates to the General Manager to implement the suggested revisions to the Code of Meeting Practice.

The Council moved into open council, the time being 06:10pm.

The General Manager Read aloud in open council:
  • 22.2 CONFIDENTIAL - Sale of Land - 4 Carmine Munro Avenue, Moree Gateway 

That Council:

  1. Notes its previous resolution to dispose of Lot 4 DP1212873 (4 Carmine Munro Avenue, Moree) and the subsequent progression of the sale process.
  2. Endorses the inclusion of a Positive Covenant on the title of Lot 4 DP1212873 requiring substantial commencement of development within the timeframe specified in the contract.
  3. Endorses the inclusion of a development bond equivalent to 10% of the purchase price as security for compliance with the Positive Covenant.
  4. Authorises the Acting General Manager to negotiate and finalise all contractual, covenant and registration arrangements necessary to give effect to the Positive Covenant and development bond.

  • 22.1 CONFIDENTIAL - Sale of Council Land: Part 175 Barton Plains Road, Moree

That Council:

  1. Endorse the sale of proposed Lot 1, being approximately 30.22 hectares of Lot 53 DP751791, Barton Plains Road Moree, generally in accordance with the proposed subdivision plan contained in Attachment 2. 
  2. Endorse the commercial terms in the draft Contract and Deed required to complete the transaction. 
  3. Delegate authority to the Acting General Manager to finalise negotiations, execute all associated documents and undertake all actions necessary to give effect to the sale. 
  4. Provide landowner's consent for the lodgement of any subdivision or development applications required to facilitate the transaction. 
  5. Authorise the affixing of Council's Seal to any documents requiring execution under seal.

 3.  Not call tenders for the hire of the plant under Section 55 (3) (i) of the Local Government Act due to the extenuating circumstances outlined in the report

That Council:
1. In line with community feedback and concerns surrounding the 50m pool, received via social media, through email, and contact with Councillors, pause any further Taylor Oval progress in relation to the 50m pool until all below concerns are satisfied.

2. Funding Clarification
Direct the General Manager to urgently seek formal written confirmation from all relevant funding bodies, including the Federal Government, NSW Government and other funding bodies, as to:
a) Whether the existing grant funding allocated for the 50m pool project can be applied to an alternative site outside of the Moree Artesian Aquatic Centre (MAAC);
b) Any conditions, restrictions, or variations required to enable such a transfer;
c) Any risks associated with loss, reduction, or delay of funding should the project be relocated.
d) Disclosure of funding sources currently being used for assessments, tender advertisements, surveying, staff time committed to moving the 50m pool to the proposed Taylor Oval site
e) Confirmation that Grant Funding specifically sourced for projects at the MAAC have not been used to pursue the Taylor Oval site.

3. Public Disclosure
That the written responses received from funding bodies be:
(a) Reported to Council at the earliest opportunity; and
(b) Made publicly available to ensure transparency for the community.

4. Comparative Assessment Requirement
That prior to any final decision regarding relocation of the 50m pool, Council be provided with a detailed report including:
a) A full cost comparison between: Completion of the 50m pool at MAAC; and Construction at any alternative site
b) Implications for existing grant funding under both scenarios;
c) Project timelines, including approval and delivery risks at both locations; noting that funding is due to be spent by December 2027
d) Any additional financial exposure to Council resulting from relocation, including potential local business detriment.
e) Proof of consultation with businesses and private land holders within the development vicinity of both locations.
f) Public Consultation undertaken and;
g) Outline the proposed timeline and how deliverables will be achieved before funding ceases.
h) That the funding for the assessment come from any remaining funds associated with the MAAC redevelopment and if funds are depleted that they be sourced from the Tourism & Economic Development Fund (TED).

5. Contractor Engagement Review
That Council receive a report outlining:
a) Whether original contractors engaged for the MAAC project were formally provided acceptance of tender and if following project disruption and the finalisation of the 3 million dollar hot pool refurbishment; they have been re contacted to determine project delivery possibilities and verified risks associated with any development of a 50m pool at the MAAC site.
b) What alternative delivery models (including staged works or split contracts) were explored;
c) Market feedback regarding delivery of the project at MAAC versus a new site.
d) Disclose who proposed that the 50m pool could not be built at the MAAC site, their qualifications and knowledge and why any alternate views were not thoroughly investigated.

6. Deferral of Irreversible Decisions
That Council refrain from making any irreversible commitment to relocate the 50m pool project until:
a) Funding applicability has been formally confirmed in writing; and
b) The above mentioned reports have been considered by Council.

7. Assessment Report
That Council
a) be provided with an assessment report outlining the economic impact on local businesses, particularly those surrounding the MAAC precinct, as a result of prolonged closure and any proposed relocation of the 50m pool and that the assessment include analysis of the impact on social cohesion of a night time, in particular at closing times due to its proximity to the main CBD area should the 50m pool be approved to be relocated to Taylor Oval.
b) That the funding for the assessment come from any remaining funds associated with the MAAC redevelopment and if funds are depleted that they be sourced from the Tourism & Economic Development Fund.

Lost

That Council:

    2. The Operational Plan and Budget 2026-2027,
    3. The Resource Strategy, Long Term Financial Plan, Asset Management Plan and Updated Workforce Management Strategy.

    2. Events Partnership Fund - $20,000.00
    3. Economic Development strategy/Implementation - $50,000.00
    4. Taylor Oval Pool Project - $250,000.00
  3. Resolves the following costs, included in the Operational Plan & Budget, be funded from Development Contribution Section 7.12 Reserve:
    1. Animal Management Facility - $1,000,000.00
    2. Mungindi Junior Rugby League Building - $500,000.00
    3. Moree Civic Precinct Green Project - $35,000.00
  4. Resolves the following costs, included in the Operational Plan & Budget, be funded from the Waste Reserve:
    1. Biniguy Transfer Station Facility - $167,725.00

    3. Rollover unused budget from 2025-2026- Increase Action 1.2.3.1 - Off Leash Dog Park - Exp $200,000.00 (Total project Exp $350K)
    4. Rollover unused budget from 2025-2026- Add New Action - Kirkby Parks Upgrade - Exp $330,000.00 (Total project Exp $330K)
    5. Rollover unused budget from 2025-2026- Increase Recurrent Landfill Budget - Landfill Capital Upgrades - Exp $114,000.00 
    6. Rollover unused budget from 2025-2026- Action 3.1.6.5 - Biniguy Transfer Station Facility - Exp $59,904.00 & Rev $59,904.00 (Total project Exp $527,147k & Rev $359,422k) 
    7. Rollover unused budget from 2025-2026- Add New Action - Treatment works Augmentation - Exp $35,000.00 (Total project Exp $35k)
    8. Rollover unused budget from 2025-2026- Add New Action - Mungindi GAB Bore rehabilitation - Exp $250,000.00 (Total project Exp $250K)
    9. Rollover unused budget from 2025-2026- Add New Action - Dilapidated Properties Clean-up and Enforcement - Exp $500,000.00 & Rev $500,000.00 (Total project Exp $500K & Rev $500k)
    10. New budget required - Add New Action - Civic Precinct Hall Concrete Driveway - Exp $60,000.00 (Total project Exp $60k)
    11. New budget required - Add New Action - Truck wash Subdivision - Exp $60,000.00 (Total project Exp $60K)
    12. Amend the level of service for publishing the recording of the council meetings to be within one day of the council meeting 
  6. Adopt proposed changes to the Revenue Policy:
    1. Accrual of Interest on Rates, Charges & Debtors from 10.50% to 9.50%
  7. Adopt proposed changes to the Long Term Financial Plan 2027-2037:
    1. Any changes required due to other recommendations included in this report
    2. Accrual of Interest on Rates, Charges & Debtors from 10.50% to 9.50%
    3. Update Cashflow to reflect estimated changes to year end cash & investment balances 
    4. Update wording in section 3.5.3 (Sewer Fund) & 6.1.3 (Unrestricted current ratio) as per attachment 7d.
  8. Adopt proposed changes to the Fees and Charges as per attachment 8.
  9. Adopt the Delivery Program 2025-2029 and DRAFT Operational Plan and Budget 2026-2027 and Resource Strategy: Long Term Financial Plan 2027-2037, Asset Management Plan and Workforce Management Strategy.
  10. Bring a report to the council at the July 2026 council meeting following a workshop to collect amendments to the action items in the operational plan

Carried

That the motion relating to Report 18.4, Transition of Tourism Moree to Moree Plains Shire Council, be put.

Carried

2026/6/15 LOST MOTION (MOVED: Councillor Cassells / SECONDED: Councillor Pearse)

That Council:
  1. Endorse the transition of tourism services from Tourism Moree into Council operations over a period not exceeding six months, in general accordance with the Tourism Transition Framework included in Attachment 1.
  2. Direct the Acting General Manager or delegate to directly engage with Tourism Moree to work collaboratively on a transition process.
  3. Receive a further report in August 2026 outlining transition progress, key risks and any remaining matters required to complete the transition.
  4. Authorise the Acting General Manager to undertake all actions necessary to facilitate the transition process. 
  5. Delegate authority to the Acting General Manager to negotiate a deed of extension of the funding agreement between Tourism Moree and Council for a period of 6 months ending December 2026, with the pro rata funding of up to $285,000 plus GST
Lost

2026/6/16 LOST MOTION (MOVED: Councillor James / SECONDED: Councillor SAUER)

That Council:
  1. Retain Tourism Moree as the principal tourism organisation for the Moree Plains Shire and not proceed with the transition of tourism services into Council operations at this time.
  2. Request a report to Council outlining options to strengthen governance, accountability, reporting requirements and performance measures for Tourism Moree while maintaining its independent industry-led structure.
  3. Endorse the development of clear Key Performance Indicators for Tourism Moree for the period July 2026 to December 2027, including measurable targets relating to visitor numbers, event attraction, marketing outcomes, stakeholder engagement and economic impact.

  5. Receive a further report by December 2026 reviewing Tourism Moree’s performance against the adopted Key Performance Indicators and assessing whether any future governance changes are warranted.
  6. Authorise the Acting General Manager to work collaboratively with Tourism Moree and relevant industry stakeholders to implement the above measures.
Lost

That Council, pursuant to Section 535 of the Local Government Act 1993 (the Act), make the following rates and charges for the 2026/2027 rating period:
1. Make the General Rates
In accordance with Section 494 of the Local Government Act 1993, Council make and levy the following ordinary rates for the year 1 July 2026 to 30 June 2027, 
a) Make a Residential Rate 
Residential Ad Valorem rate (to apply to rateable land categorised as Residential within Moree Plains Shire in accordance with Section 516 of the Act) of 0.01147352 cents in the dollar and having a base rate of $500 per assessment (representing 17.13% of the total yield in accordance with Section 500 of the Act), yielding a total income of $4,999,089 in compliance with Council's allowable Notional Income.   
b) Make a Residential Rural Rate 
Residential Rural Ad Valorem rate (to apply to all rateable land Sub-categorised Residential Rural within Moree Plains Shire in accordance with Section 529 (2)(b) of the Act) of 0.01147352 cents in the dollar and having a base rate of $500 per assessment (representing 2.78% of the total yield in accordance with Section 500 of the Act), yielding a total income of $811,226 in compliance with Council's allowable Notional Income.
 c) Make a Business Moree Rate
Business Moree Ad Valorem rate (to apply to all rateable land sub-categorised Business Moree within Moree Plains Shire in accordance with Section 529(2)(d) of the Act) of 0.03586841 cents in the dollar and having a base rate of $500 (representing 11.16% of the total yield in accordance with Section 500 of the Act), yielding a total income of $3,256,823 in compliance with Council’s allowable Notional Income.   
d) Make a Business Rate 
Business Ad Valorem rate (to apply to all rateable land categorised Business within Moree Plains Shire in accordance with Section 518 of the Act) of 0.00842358 cents in the dollar and having a base rate of $500 (representing 0.64% of the total income in accordance with Section 500 of the Act), yielding a total income of $188,165 in compliance with Council's allowable Notional Income. 
 e) Make a Farmland Rate 
Farmland Ad Valorem rate (to apply to all rateable land categorised as Farmland within Moree Plains Shire in accordance with Section 515 of the Act) of 0.00166884 cents in the dollar and having a base rate of $500 per assessment (representing 66.77% of the total yield in accordance with Section 500 of the Act), yielding a total income of $19,489,809 in compliance with Council's Allowable Notional Income.
 f) Make a Mining Rate
Mining Ad Valorem rate (to apply to all rateable land categorised as Mining within Moree Plains Shire in accordance with Section 515) of 2.87370000 cents in the dollar and having a base rate of $20,000 per assessment (representing 0% of the total yield in accordance with Section 500 of the Act), yielding a total income of $0 in compliance with Council's Allowable Notional Income
Make a Special Rate
g) Make a Business Intensive Ginning/Receival Centre – Special Rate 
Business Intensive Ginning/Receival Centre Ad Valorem rate (to apply to all rateable land Sub-categorised Business Intensive Ginning/Receival Centre within Moree Plains Shire in accordance with Section 529(2)(d) of the Act) of 0.02841256 cents in the dollar and having a base rate of $1,360 per assessment (representing 1.53% of the total yield in accordance with Section 500 of the Act), yielding a total income of $446,515 in compliance with Council's allowable Notional Income.  
 2.     Make a Water Charge
In relation to water supply charges; in accordance with Section 501 and Section 502 of the Local Government Act 1993, Council make and levy the following charges for Water Supply Services in 2026/2027:
Make an Availability Charge:
  1. Charge each parcel of separately valued land one availability charge per annum of $298.07 for each Council connected water meter for residential customers that have a 20mm, 25mm or 32mm connection. 
  2. Charge vacant land without a water meter an availability charge is $149.04 (which is 50% of the current residential availability charge). Residents with a larger connection will pay an access charge based on the following non-residual charges.
  3. Non-Residential Water Availability Charge 20mm connection $298.07
  4. Non-Residential Water Availability Charge 25mm connection $465.74
  5. Non-Residential Water Availability Charge 32mm connection $763.06
  6. Residential and Non-Residential Water Availability Charge 40mm connection $1,192.28
  7. Residential and Non-Residential Water Availability Charge 50mm connection $1,862.94
  8. Residential and Non-Residential Water Availability Charge 80mm connection $4,769.13
  9. Residential and Non-Residential Water Availability Charge 100mm connection $7,451.77
  10. Residential and Non-Residential Water Availability Charge 150mm connection $16,766.49
  11. Residential and Non-Residential Water Availability Charge 200mm connection $29,807.09

 Make a Water Consumption Charge
 In relation to water consumption charges; pursuant to Section 502 of the Local Government Act make the following charges for 2026/2027
 
 a. Potable Water Consumption Charge of $1.98 per KL up to 750 KL per annum (known as tier 1)
 b. Potable Water Consumption Charge of $2.91 per KL above 750 KL per annum (known as tier 2
 c. Non-Potable Water Consumption Charge of $1.32 per KL up to 750 KL per annum (known as tier 1)
 d. Non-Potable Water Consumption Charge of $1.94 per KL above 750 KL per annum (known as tier 2)
3. Make a Sewer Charge
In relation to sewerage service charges; in accordance with Section 501 and Section 502 of the Local Government Act 1993, Council make and levy the charges for Sewerage Services in 2026/2027 as follows:
  1. Residential sewer charges will consist of one flat tariff of $877.61
  2. All non-residential properties will be charged based on a two-tier pricing system. Sewer charges will be in accordance with Best Practice Pricing guidelines, which prescribes an availability charge based upon the corresponding water meter connection size. The Sewerage Discharge Factor is charged at a per kilolitre usage charges of $1.59 per KL based on water usage and disposal estimates.
  3. Non-Residential Sewer Availability based on water connection 20mm $720.09
  4. Non-Residential Sewer Availability based on water connection 25mm $877.61
  5. Non-Residential Sewer Availability based on water connection 32mm $1,437.88
  6. Non-Residential Sewer Availability based on water connection 40mm $2,246.69
  7. Non-Residential Sewer Availability based on water connection 50mm $3,510.45

That Council adopt the Financial Sustainability Policy.

Carried

 

In accordance with the Local Government Act 1993 and the Local Government (General) Regulation 2021, in the opinion of the General Manager, the following business is of a kind as referred to in Section 10A(2) of the Act, and should be dealt with in a part of the meeting closed to the media and public. 

(a)      personnel matters concerning particular individuals (other than councillors),
(b)      the personal hardship of any resident or ratepayer,
(c)      information that would, if disclosed, confer a commercial advantage on a person with whom the council is conducting (or proposes to conduct) business,
(d)      commercial information of a confidential nature that would, if disclosed:
(i)       prejudice the commercial position of the person who supplied it, or
(ii)      confer a commercial advantage on a competitor of the council, or    
(iii)     reveal a trade secret,
(e)      information that would, if disclosed, prejudice the maintenance of law,
(f)       matters affecting the security of the council, councillors, council staff or council property,
(g)      advice concerning litigation, or advice that would otherwise be privileged from production in legal proceedings on the ground of legal professional privilege,
(h)      information concerning the nature and location of a place or an item of Aboriginal significance on community land,
(i)      alleged contraventions of any code of conduct requirements applicable under section 440.

2026/6/41 RESOLVED (MOVED: Councillor Tighe /SECONDED: Councillor Cassells) 

  1. That Council move into closed council to consider business identified, tabled at the meeting.
  2. That pursuant under Section 10A(1)-(3) of the Local Government Act 1993, the media and public be excluded from the meeting on the basis that the business to be considered is classified confidential under the provisions of Section 10A(2) as outlined above.
  3. That the correspondence and reports relevant to the subject business be withheld from access to the media and public as required by Section 11(2) of the Local Government Act 1993.

Carried

The Council moved into closed Council at the time being 05:52pm. The public and media left the Chamber.

  2. That Council:

  1.   2. That the Councillor's conduct, during and after the 18 December 2025 Ordinary Council Meeting, 5 February 2026 Extraordinary Council Meeting and 19 February 2026 Ordinary Council Meeting, has been found by an independent investigator to constitute a breach of the following provisions of Council's Code of Conduct:

    4. 3.22 — acts of disorder or other conduct at council meetings that are intended to prevent the proper or effective functioning of the council.

That Council:
  1. thanks the Community for their input concerning the Draft Taylor Oval Masterplan;
  2. endorses the Draft Taylor Oval Masterplan Consultation Outcomes Report, prepared by Community Insights, as the record of the outcomes of community consultation on the Draft Taylor Oval Masterplan and Stage 1;
  3. endorses the Stage 1 Master Plan to be progressed to detailed cost planning, based on the scope determined by Council, to confirm that Stage 1 can be delivered within the available project budget;
  4. endorses the inclusion of the Children’s Leisure Pool and Splash Pad, and additional shading, as part of Stage 2 of the Taylor Oval Vision 2040 Masterplan;
  5. directs the Acting General Manager to undertake a site assessment to explore the potential provision of hot artesian water to the Taylor Oval site; and
  6. directs the Acting General Manager to bring a report to Council that presents the feedback from the Aboriginal Cultural Heritage Assessment and community submissions, and considers their implications for the Taylor Oval Vision 2040 Masterplan.



AMENDMENT TO THE MOTION (MOVED: Councillor James / SECONDED: Councillor McGrady)

That Council: 

  1. thanks the Community for their input concerning the Draft Taylor Oval Masterplan;

  3. endorses the Stage 1 Master Plan to be progressed to detailed cost planning, based on the scope determined by Council, to confirm that Stage 1 can be delivered within the available project budget;
  4. endorses the inclusion of the Children’s Leisure Pool and Splash Pad, and additional shading, as part of Stage 2 of the Taylor Oval Vision 2040 Masterplan;
  5. directs the Acting General Manager to undertake a site assessment to explore the potential provision of hot artesian water to the Talyor Oval site; and
  6. directs the Acting General Manager to bring a report to Council that presents the feedback from the Aboriginal Cultural Heritage Assessment and community submissions and considers their implications for the Taylor Oval Vision 2040 Masterplan.

  2. assaults or threatens to assault another councillor or person present at the meeting, or

The Mayor, Councillor Susannah Pearse assumed the Chair.

That Council: 
  1. elect a Deputy Mayor;
  2. fix the term of office of the Deputy Mayor as equal to the Mayoral term; and
  3. elect the Deputy Mayor by way of open voting if more than one nomination for Deputy Mayor is received.

For:  Susannah Pearse, Wayne Tighe, Peter Mailler, Debra Williams, Dominique Hodgkinson, Kerry Cassells
Against: NIL
Abstain: NIL
Excused: Frederick McGrady, Kelly James, Brooke Sauer

Carried 


The General Manager advised that one (1) nomination for the position of Deputy Mayor has been received from Councillor Michael Wayne Tighe. 

The General Manager asked Councillor Michael Wayne Tighe whether he accepted the nomination, and Councillor Tighe confirmed his acceptance

The General Manager called for any further nominations. No further nominations received. 

 

The General Manager declared that Councillor Michael Wayne Tighe to be elected Deputy Mayor until September 2028.

Flood Funding

That LGNSW advocates:
  1. To the NSW Reconstruction Authority for:
    1. A maximum 30-day variation process for flood funding with a guarantee that funding will not be denied or rescinded through the process;
    2. Cash settlement of council flood claims, allowing councils to determine the best scope of work to deliver a "better off overall" result for the road in question in terms of safety and trafficability, with councils to provide acquittals for the delivered better off overall works.
  1. To the NSW Resources Regulator, the NSW Environment Protection Authority and other relevant Ministers and departments, requesting exemption of council-owned and operated gravel quarry extraction limits when supplying gravel for disaster-remediation works. 
Restoration of pre-meeting briefing sessions

That LGNSW advocates:
  1. to The Hon. Ron Hoenig, MP, Minister for Local Government, for the repeal of section 236A of the Local Government (General) Regulation 2021 (NSW); and 
  2. to the Chief Executive of the Office of Local Government for:
    1. future iterations of the Model Code of Meeting Practice for Local Councils in NSW to contain provisions that facilitate the conduct of pre-meeting briefing sessions and councillor workshops; and 
    2. the development of guidelines under section 23A of the Local Government Act 1993 (NSW) concerning the conduct of pre-meeting briefing sessions and councillor workshops.

Carried

That Council: 
  1. Acknowledges the passing of Justice Mary Gaudron KC;
  2. Recognises the extraordinary life and contributions of Justice Gaudron, from growing up in Morton Street, Moree, to becoming the first woman to become a Queen's Counsel in 1981, the first female Solicitor-General of an Australian state in 1981, and the first woman appointed to the High Court of Australia in 1987;
  3. Acknowledges the profound impact Justice Gaudron's support of equal rights had both locally and nationally, especially for Aboriginal people and women, including through the landmark Mabo (No.2) land rights decision, equal pay and maternity leave; 
  4. Extends it sincere condolences to Justice Gaudron's family, friends and all those who knew her;
  5. Endorse the Mayor and General Manager writing to relevant departments and Ministers in the NSW and Australian Governments to request the installation of a statue of Justice Gaudron at the Moree Court House, to ensure that her work and her Moree origin story are remembered for generations to come.

Carried

2026/10/1  RESOLVED (MOVED: Councillor Tighe / SECONDED: Councillor Cassells)

15.24 Without limiting clause 15.17, a contravention of clause 15.232 or an attempt to contravene that clause, constitutes disorderly conduct for the purpose of clause 15.17. Carried

 That Council move into Committee of the Whole

2026/10/24 RESOLVED (MOVED: COUNCILLOR MCGRADY / SECONDED: COUNCILLOR HODGKINSON)

That Council move out of Committee of the Whole

The Council moved out of Committee of the Whole, the time being 04:39pm.

Carried


2026/10/25 RESOLVED (MOVED: Councillor Mailler / SECONDED: Councillor Tighe)

That Council:

  1.  Note the Indicative Budget Estimate prepared by Muller Partnership for Stage 1 of the Taylor Oval Aquatic Centre (Stage 1).
  2.  Note the draft Project Governance Framework for the development and delivery of Stage 1.
  3.  Appoint the Mayor as the Chair and a member of the Taylor Oval Aquatic Centre Project Steering Committee.
  4.  Appoint Councillors Tighe, Cassells, Williams, Sauer to serve, in addition to the Mayor, as members of the Taylor Oval Aquatic Centre Project Steering Committee.
  5.  Invite the Moree Local Aboriginal Land Council, Moree Amateur Swimming Club, Moree Diggers Swimming Club, Tourism Moree Inc and the Moree & District Chamber of Commerce to each nominate one representative to serve as a member of the Taylor Oval Aquatic Centre Project Steering Committee. 
  6. Call for nominations from the community for up to three individuals with relevant aquatic centre management or construction experience to serve as members of the Taylor Oval Aquatic Centre Project Steering Committee.
  7. Direct the Acting General Manager to present a report to the November Ordinary Council Meeting that:
    1. facilitates consideration of the nominations received in response to (5) and (6), together with a draft Terms of Reference for the Taylor Oval Aquatic Centre Project Steering Committee; and 
    2. presents an updated Project Governance Framework for the development and delivery of Stage 1.
  1. Note that a procurement process to source a suitably qualified and experienced client-side Project Manager in respect of Stage 1 is in progress.
  1.  Direct the Acting General Manager to present a further report to Council to facilitate Council’s selection of a client-side Project Manager in respect of Stage 1.
  2. Endorse Stage 1 of the Taylor Oval Aquatic Centre to progress subject to Heritage NSW advice. 
  3.  Direct the Acting General Manager to commence an appropriate procurement process to source a suitably qualified and experienced contractor for the design and construction of Stage 1. 
  4.  Direct the Acting General Manager to present a further report to Council to facilitate consideration of tenders received for the design and construction of Stage 1.

Carried
